title.zh: 卷十五 魏書十五 劉司馬梁張溫賈傳
title.en: Volume 15: Book of Wei 15 - Biographies of Liu, Sima, Liang, Zhang, Wen, and Jia
title.raw: 卷十五 魏書十五 劉司馬梁張溫賈傳 Volume 15: Book of Wei 15 - Biographies of Liu, Sima, Liang, Zhang, Wen, and Jia

sentences.zh: 劉馥字元穎，沛國相人也。

translations.literal: Liu Fu, courtesy name Yuanying, was a native of Xiang in the Principality of Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fu, style Yuanying, hailed from Xiang in Pei commandery.

sentences.zh: 避亂揚州，建安初，說袁術將戚寄、秦翊，使率衆與俱詣太祖。

translations.literal: He fled turmoil to Yangzhou; at the beginning of the Jian'an era he persuaded Yuan Shu's generals Qi Ji and Qin Yi to lead their masses and go with him to visit the Grand Progenitor (Cao Cao).
translations.idiomatic: He took refuge from the disorder in Yangzhou. Early in the Jian'an reign he talked Yuan Shu's officers Qi Ji and Qin Yi into bringing their troops with him to join Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 太祖恱之，司徒辟為掾。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor was pleased with him; the Minister of Education summoned him as a clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao took a liking to him, and the minister of education appointed him a staff clerk.

sentences.zh: 後孫策所置廬江太守李述攻殺揚州刺史嚴象，廬江梅乾、雷緒、陳蘭等聚衆數萬在江、淮間，郡縣殘破。

translations.literal: Later Li Shu, the Administrator of Lujiang installed by Sun Ce, attacked and killed the Inspector of Yangzhou Yan Xiang; Mei Gan, Lei Xu, Chen Lan, and others of Lujiang gathered a host in the tens of thousands between the Yangzi and the Huai, and the commanderies and counties lay in ruins.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Lujiang prefect Li Shu, whom Sun Ce had put in office, attacked and killed Yangzhou Inspector Yan Xiang; Mei Gan, Lei Xu, Chen Lan, and others from Lujiang raised tens of thousands of followers between the Yangzi and the Huai, and commandery after commandery was broken and laid waste.

sentences.zh: 太祖方有袁紹之難，謂馥可任以東南之事，遂表為揚州刺史。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor was then facing the crisis with Yuan Shao; he deemed Fu fit to be entrusted with affairs in the southeast, and therefore memorialized appointing him Inspector of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao was then mired in his struggle with Yuan Shao; judging Liu Fu capable of handling the southeast, he memorialized the throne and had him named Inspector of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 馥旣受命，單馬造合肥空城，建立州治，南懷緒等，皆安集之，貢獻相繼。

translations.literal: Fu having received his commission, rode alone to the empty city of Hefei, established the seat of the inspectorate, treated Lei Xu and the others in the south with kindness, all settled them, and tribute arrived in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Once Liu Fu had his orders, he rode alone into the empty city of Hefei, set up the provincial government, won over Lei Xu and the bands to the south, brought them all peacefully under his authority, and tribute from the region began to flow in without interruption.

sentences.zh: 數年中恩化大行，百姓樂其政，流民越江山而歸者以萬數。

translations.literal: Within several years his grace and transforming influence were broadly felt; the common people rejoiced in his government, and displaced persons who crossed rivers and mountains to return were counted by the ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In a few years the beneficent sway of his rule was everywhere felt; the people welcomed his administration, and refugees who crossed mountains and rivers to come home numbered in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 於是聚諸生，立學校，廣屯田，興治芍陂及茹陂、七門、吳塘諸堨以溉稻田，官民有畜。

translations.literal: Thereupon he gathered the students, established schools, widely opened up military-agricultural colonies, had Shaoyi, Ruyi, Qimen, and Wutang dikes raised and regulated to irrigate paddy fields, and both officials and civilians had stores.
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned literati, founded schools, expanded the military-colony system, and had the Shaoyi, Ruyi, Qimen, and Wutang embankments built up and regulated to irrigate the paddies, so that officials and commoners alike had surplus stored away.

sentences.zh: 又高為城壘，多積木石，編作草苫數千萬枚，益貯魚膏數千斛，為戰守備。

translations.literal: He further raised the height of the walls and ramparts, stocked great quantities of timber and stone, wove straw matting by the tens of millions of pieces, and increased stores of fish oil by several thousand hu as preparations for battle and defense.
translations.idiomatic: He likewise raised the city's walls and towers, stockpiled timber and stone, plaited millions of bundles of straw matting, and laid in thousands of hu of fish oil—all to ready Hefei for siege and defense.

sentences.zh: 建安十三年卒。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jian'an he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirteenth year of Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 孫權率十萬衆攻圍合肥城百餘日，時天連雨，城欲崩，於是以苫蓑覆之，夜然脂照城外，視賊所作而為備，賊以破走。

translations.literal: Sun Quan led a host of one hundred thousand to attack and besiege the city of Hefei for more than a hundred days; at the time the rains fell continuously and the wall was about to collapse, so they covered it with matting and rush thatch, at night burned grease to illuminate outside the wall, observed what the enemy was doing and made preparations accordingly, and the enemy broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan brought a hundred thousand men to invest Hefei for over a hundred days. Rain fell without ceasing until the walls threatened to give way; the defenders shored them with mats and thatch, and at night burned lard-oil lamps along the parapet to study the enemy's works and counter them. The attackers eventually broke and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 揚州士民益追思之，以為雖董安于之守晉陽，不能過也。

translations.literal: The scholars and commoners of Yangzhou all the more recalled him fondly, thinking that even Dong Anyu's defense of Jinyang could not surpass it.
translations.idiomatic: The gentry and common folk of Yangzhou remembered him with increasing admiration, convinced that even Dong Anyu's storied defense of Jinyang had not surpassed what Liu Fu had left them.

sentences.zh: 及陂塘之利，至今為用。

translations.literal: As for the benefit of the reservoirs and dikes, down to the present they remain in use.
translations.idiomatic: The irrigation works he began are still doing their work today.

sentences.zh: 子 靖

translations.literal: Son: Jing
translations.idiomatic: Son: Liu Jing

sentences.zh: 〈《晉陽秋》曰：劉弘字叔和，熙之弟也。

translations.literal: The Jin Yangchun says: Liu Hong, courtesy name Shuhe, was the younger brother of Xi.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Jin Yangchun, Liu Hong, courtesy name Shuhe, was the younger brother of Liu Xi.

sentences.zh: 弘與晉世祖同年，居同里，以舊恩屢登顯位。

translations.literal: Hong was the same age as Jin Shizu and lived in the same lane; by old friendship he repeatedly rose to eminent positions.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong had been born the same year as Sima Yan and had grown up on the same street; those longstanding ties lifted him again and again to high office.

sentences.zh: 自靖至弘，世不曠名，而有政事才。

translations.literal: From Jing down to Hong, for generations the family name was never empty, and they had administrative talent.
translations.idiomatic: From Liu Jing through Liu Hong no generation lacked a name worth remembering, and each showed a gift for practical government.

sentences.zh: 晉西朝之末，弘為車騎大將軍開府，荊州刺史，假節都督荊、交、廣州諸軍事，封新城郡公。

translations.literal: Near the end of the Western Jin, Hong became General of Chariots and Cavalry with a separate headquarters, Governor of Jingzhou, with ceremonial credentials and command over the military affairs of Jing, Jiao, and Guang provinces, and was enfeoffed Duke of Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Toward the close of the Western Jin, Liu Hong rose to general of chariots and cavalry with an independent command, governor of Jingzhou, bearer of the imperial baton as military overseer of Jing, Jiao, and Guang, and was invested duke of Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 其在江、漢，值王室多難，得專命一方，盡其器能。

translations.literal: When he was on the Yangzi and Han, it happened that the royal house faced many difficulties; he obtained sole authority over one quarter and fully employed his capacity.
translations.idiomatic: While he held the Yangzi and Han basins, the imperial house was beset by crises; he was left to rule his corner of the realm on his own authority and used every ounce of his ability.

sentences.zh: 推誠羣下，厲以公義，簡刑獄，務農桑。

translations.literal: He put sincerity forth to those below him, encouraged them with impartial righteousness, simplified punishments and prisons, and urged farming and sericulture.
translations.idiomatic: He dealt openly with his subordinates, spurred them with a sense of public duty, lightened penal administration, and pressed the planting of grain and the raising of silkworms.

sentences.zh: 每有興發，手書郡國，丁寧款密，故莫不感恱，顛倒奔赴，咸曰「得劉公一紙書，賢於十部從事也」。

translations.literal: Whenever there was a project to undertake, he personally wrote letters to the commanderies and kingdoms, earnestly and in detail, so that none failed to be moved and pleased; they scrambled to hasten to him, all saying, "To obtain one sheet from Lord Liu is better than ten departmental aides."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he needed something done, he drafted personal letters to every commandery and kingdom, careful and warm in tone, so that his officials were never anything but eager to respond; they used to say that a single note from Liu Hong was worth more than ten staff supervisors.

sentences.zh: 時帝在長安，命弘得選用宰守。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor was at Chang'an and ordered Hong to be able to select and appoint prefects and governors.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven was then at Chang'an and authorized Liu Hong to appoint his own magistrates and governors.

sentences.zh: 徵士武陵伍朝高尚其事，牙門將皮初有勳江漢，弘上朝為零陵太守，初為襄陽太守。

translations.literal: The summoned gentleman Wu Chao of Wuling took high-minded retirement as his way, and Ya General Pi Chu had merit on the Jiang and Han; Hong recommended Chao as Administrator of Lingling and Chu as Administrator of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: The recluse Wu Chao of Wuling had chosen a life of lofty seclusion, while the ya-general Pi Chu had distinguished himself along the Jiang and Han; Liu Hong recommended Wu Chao for Lingling and Pi Chu for Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 詔書以襄陽顯郡，初資名輕淺，以弘壻夏侯陟為襄陽。

translations.literal: The edict said that Xiangyang was a prominent commandery; Chu's qualifications and reputation were slight and shallow, and therefore made Hong's son-in-law Xiahou Zhi administrator of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: The rescript replied that Xiangyang was too important a seat for Pi Chu, whose rank and reputation were modest, and named Liu Hong's son-in-law Xiahou Zhi to the post instead.

sentences.zh: 弘曰：「夫統天下者當與天下同心，治一國者當與一國推實。

translations.literal: Hong said: "He who rules the All-under-Heaven ought to share one mind with the All-under-Heaven; he who governs one state ought to promote substance with one state.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong said, "Whoever holds the realm must think with the whole realm; whoever tends a single kingdom must seek true merit with all who serve it.

sentences.zh: 吾統荊州十郡，安得十女壻，然後為治哉！

translations.literal: If I rule ten commanderies of Jingzhou, how could I obtain ten sons-in-law and only then govern!"
translations.idiomatic: I oversee ten commanderies in Jingzhou—am I supposed to need ten sons-in-law before I can govern them fairly!"

sentences.zh: 」乃表「陟姻親，舊制不得相監臨事，初勳宜見酬」。

translations.literal: Thereupon he memorialized: "Zhi is related by marriage; by old regulations one may not mutually supervise; Chu's merit ought to be rewarded."
translations.idiomatic: He therefore memorialized: "Because Xiahou Zhi is my kinsman by marriage, precedent forbids his holding supervisory authority over me; Pi Chu's service deserves recognition."

sentences.zh: 報聽之，衆益服其公當。

translations.literal: The reply granted it; the multitude all the more admired his fairness and fitness.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved his plea, and the world only admired him the more for his even-handed justice.

sentences.zh: 廣漢太守辛冉以天子蒙塵，四方雲擾，進從橫計於弘。

translations.literal: Xin Ran, the Administrator of Guanghan, because the Son of Heaven was covered in dust and the four quarters were like swirling clouds, advanced stratagems of maneuver to Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Ran of Guanghan, seeing the emperor driven from his capital and the empire in turmoil, pressed on Liu Hong a scheme of opportunist ambition.

sentences.zh: 弘怒斬之，時人莫不稱善。

translations.literal: Hong angrily executed him; at the time none did not praise it as good.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong had him put to death in anger; contemporaries unanimously applauded the deed.

sentences.zh: 《晉諸公贊》曰：于時天下雖亂，荊州安全。

translations.literal: The Jin Zhugong zan says: At that time though the empire was in disorder, Jingzhou remained secure.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin Zhugong zan observes that while the realm was falling apart, Jingzhou alone stayed calm.

sentences.zh: 弘有劉景升保有江漢之志，不附太傅司馬越。

translations.literal: Hong had the intention of Liu Jingsheng in preserving the Jiang and Han, and did not attach himself to Grand Tutor Sima Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong harbored something of Liu Biao's old dream of holding the Jiang and Han as a shield; he refused to throw in his lot with the grand tutor Sima Yue.

sentences.zh: 越甚銜之。

translations.literal: Yue deeply bore a grudge against him.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue nursed a deep grudge against him for it.

sentences.zh: 會弘病卒。

translations.literal: It happened that Hong died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Before matters could come to a head, Liu Hong fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 子璠，北中郎將。〉

translations.literal: Son Fan, North General of the Middle.
translations.idiomatic: His son Liu Fan rose to north general of the central armies.

sentences.zh: 司馬朗

translations.literal: Sima Lang
translations.idiomatic: Sima Lang

sentences.zh: 司馬朗字伯達，河内溫人也。

translations.literal: Sima Lang, courtesy name Boda, was a native of Wen in Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Lang, courtesy name Boda, was a man of Wen in Henei.

sentences.zh: 〈司馬彪序傳曰：朗祖父雋，字元異，博學好古，倜儻有大度。

translations.literal: Sima Biao's Prefatory Biography says: Lang's grandfather Jun, courtesy name Yuanyi, was broadly learned and fond of antiquity, untrammeled and possessed of great composure.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Biao's preface to the family history relates that Sima Lang's grandfather Jun, style Yuanyi, was erudite, loved the classics of antiquity, carried himself with unstudied grandeur, and had uncommon breadth of spirit.

sentences.zh: 長八尺三寸，腰帶十圍，儀狀魁岸，與眾有異，鄉黨宗族咸景附焉。

translations.literal: He was eight chi three cun in height; his girdle took ten rounds; his bearing was lofty in appearance and differed from the multitude; his village, clan, and kin all looked up to him as to a mountain and attached themselves.
translations.idiomatic: He stood eight feet three inches tall, his waist required a belt ten spans around, and his frame towered over other men; kinsmen and neighbors alike gathered beneath him as to a peak.

sentences.zh: 位至穎川太守。

translations.literal: He rose to the position of Administrator of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He ascended as far as prefect of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 父防，字建公，性質直公方，雖閑居宴處，威儀不忒。

translations.literal: His father Fang, courtesy name Jiangong, was by nature honest, upright, and square; though at leisure in feasting and dwelling, his awesome demeanor did not deviate.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sima Fang, style Jiangong, was blunt, equitable, and exacting: even at home among family feasts his deportment never slipped.

sentences.zh: 雅好《漢書名臣列傳》，所諷誦者數十萬言。

translations.literal: He elegantly loved the Han shu Mingchen liezhuan; what he recited from it numbered in the hundreds of thousands of characters.
translations.idiomatic: He doted on the Han shu's chapters on famous ministers and could chant several hundred thousand characters from them by heart.

sentences.zh: 少仕州郡，歷官洛陽令、京兆尹，以年老轉拜骑都尉。

translations.literal: In youth he served prefectures and commanderies, passing through offices as Magistrate of Luoyang and Governor of the capital region; in old age he was transferred and appointed Colonel Commandant of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career in local posts, served as magistrate of Luoyang and governor of the capital district, and in his later years was rotated into the position of colonel of cavalry.

sentences.zh: 養志閭巷，闔門自守。

translations.literal: He nourished his aims in the lanes and alleys, closing his gate and guarding himself.
translations.idiomatic: In retirement he cultivated his mind behind closed doors, mixing little with the world.

sentences.zh: 諸子雖冠成人，不命曰進不敢進，不命曰坐不敢坐，不指有所問不敢言，父子之間肅如也。

translations.literal: Though his sons had passed the capping rite and reached adulthood, unless ordered to advance they did not dare advance; unless ordered to sit they did not dare sit; unless something was pointed out and inquired of they did not dare speak; between father and sons it was solemn as a court.
translations.idiomatic: Even after his sons came of age, none might step forward until summoned to come forward, none might sit until told to sit, none might speak until addressed; the distance between father and sons was as formal as a court audience.

sentences.zh: 年七十一，建安二十四年終。

translations.literal: At age seventy-one, he died in the twenty-fourth year of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-one in the twenty-fourth year of Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 有子八人，朗最長，次即晉宣皇帝也。〉

translations.literal: He had eight sons; Lang was the eldest, and the next was the Jin Emperor Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Fang left eight sons, Sima Lang the eldest and the future Emperor Xuan of Jin, Sima Yi, the next.

sentences.zh: 九歲，人有道其父字者，朗曰：「慢人親者，不敬其親者也。

translations.literal: At age nine, when someone spoke his father's courtesy name, Lang said: "He who slights another's parents does not respect his own parents."
translations.idiomatic: When he was nine, a guest used his father's courtesy name. Sima Lang replied, "Anyone who insults another man's parents cannot be honoring his own."

sentences.zh: 」客謝之。

translations.literal: The guest apologized to him.
translations.idiomatic: The visitor apologized.

sentences.zh: 十二，試經爲童子郎，監試者以其身體壮大，疑朗匿年，劾問。

translations.literal: At twelve, tested on the classics he became a boy gentleman; the examiner, because his body was large and strong, suspected Lang of concealing his years and impeached and questioned him.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he passed the classics examination for "child cadet" candidacy; the proctor, struck by his height and bulk, suspected him of lying about his age and formally challenged him.

sentences.zh: 朗曰：「朗之内外，累世長大，朗雖穉弱，無仰高之風，損年以求早成，非志所爲也。

translations.literal: Lang said: "Lang's inner and outer kin for generations have been large of frame; though Lang is young and weak, I have no lofty airs, and to diminish my years seeking early accomplishment is not what my will would do."
translations.idiomatic: Sima Lang answered, "Men on both sides of my family have been tall for generations. I may be young, but I am not precocious; shaving years off my life story to get ahead early is not what I intend."

sentences.zh: 」監試者異之。

translations.literal: The examiner marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: The examiner conceded the point with admiration.

sentences.zh: 後關東兵起，故冀州刺史李邵家居野王，近山險，欲徙居溫。

translations.literal: Later when the armies east of the pass arose, the former Inspector of Ji Province Li Shao, dwelling in Yewang near mountainous defiles, wished to move residence to Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as armies rose east of the passes, the former Ji inspector Li Shao, who lived in Yewang near rugged hills, planned to relocate his household to the safer town of Wen.

sentences.zh: 朗謂邵曰：「脣齒之喻，豈唯虞、虢，溫與野王即是也；

translations.literal: Lang said to Shao: "The metaphor of lips and teeth—is it only Yu and Guo? Wen and Yewang are just that case;
translations.idiomatic: Sima Lang told him, "The lips-and-teeth proverb does not apply only to ancient Yu and Guo—Yewang and Wen stand in exactly that relationship;

sentences.zh: 今去彼而居此，是爲避朝亡之期耳。

translations.literal: now to leave that and dwell here is to flee the time of the court's demise."
translations.idiomatic: to abandon Yewang for Wen is simply to run from one impending collapse toward another."

sentences.zh: 且君，國人之望也，今寇未至而先徙，帶山之縣必駭，是摇動民之心而開姦宄之原也，竊爲郡内憂之。

translations.literal: Moreover you are what the people of the state look to; now before the bandits arrive you move first; the counties along the mountains will surely be alarmed—this is shaking the people's hearts and opening the source of villainy; I privately worry for the sake of the commandery interior.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover you are the man the county looks to; if you bolt before the enemy appears, every hill district along the border will panic—you would unsettle the people and invite every malcontent to move. For the commandery's sake I dread the thought."

sentences.zh: 」邵不從。

translations.literal: Shao did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shao would not listen.

sentences.zh: 邊山之民果亂，内徙，或爲寇鈔。

translations.literal: The people along the border mountains indeed rebelled, moved inward, or became bandit raiders.
translations.idiomatic: Sure enough the upland communities rose in disorder, drifted inward, or turned to pillage.

sentences.zh: 是時董卓遷天子都長安，卓因留洛陽。

translations.literal: At this time Dong Zhuo moved the Son of Heaven's capital to Chang'an; Zhuo therefore remained at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Dong Zhuo had transferred the imperial seat to Chang'an while he himself stayed on in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 朗父防爲治書御史，當徙西，以四方雲擾，乃遣朗將家屬還本縣。

translations.literal: Lang's father Fang was Clerk Compiler of Documents and ought to have moved west; because the four quarters were like swirling clouds, he sent Lang leading the family dependents back to their home county.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Fang, then a senior clerical official bound for the western capital, saw chaos everywhere and sent Sima Lang home at the head of the household instead.

sentences.zh: 或有告朗欲逃亡者，執以詣卓，卓謂朗曰：「卿與吾亡兒同歲，幾大相負！

translations.literal: Someone reported Lang as intending to flee; he was seized and brought to Zhuo; Zhuo said to Lang: "You are the same age as my late son; how greatly you have failed me!"
translations.idiomatic: An informer accused Sima Lang of planning to abscond; he was arrested and hauled before Dong Zhuo, who said, "You are the same age as my dead son—how deeply you disappoint me!"

sentences.zh: 」朗因曰：「明公以高世之德，遭陽九之會，清除羣穢，廣舉賢士，此誠虚心垂慮，將興至治也。

translations.literal: Lang thereupon said: "The enlightened lord, with virtue that towers above the age, has encountered the nine-in-the-tally crisis, clears away the swarming filth, and widely promotes worthy gentlemen—this is truly emptying the mind and letting cares hang down, about to raise the utmost good government."
translations.idiomatic: Sima Lang replied, "You bear an ambition loftier than the times; fate has dealt you the harshest lot, yet you scourge corruption and promote the worthy—a sure sign you mean to found a reign of true peace."

sentences.zh: 威德以隆，功業以著，而兵難日起，州郡鼎沸，郊境之内，民不安業，捐棄居產，流亡藏竄，雖四關設禁，重加刑戮，猶不絕息，此朗之所以於邑也。

translations.literal: Your awesome virtue rises daily, merit and enterprise are manifest, yet military disasters arise daily, commanderies and prefectures boil like tripods, within the borders of the capital region the people do not rest secure in their occupations, abandon dwellings and property, flee and hide and scatter—though the four passes set prohibitions and punishments are doubled and executions added, still it does not cease and rest—this is why Lang is sorrowful within."
translations.idiomatic: Your prestige spreads and your achievements shine, yet war flares day after day, every region seethes, and inside the capital district men cannot tend their farms or homes—they leave houses and fields empty and scatter into hiding. Not even blockades on every frontier nor doubled penalties can stop the exodus. That is what rends my heart."

sentences.zh: 願明公監觀往事，少加三思，即榮名並於日月，伊、周不足侔也。

translations.literal: I hope the enlightened lord will inspect and observe past affairs, slightly add three times reflection, then glorious name will stand together with sun and moon, and Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou will not be enough to match."
translations.idiomatic: If you would study the lessons of history and think thrice on each step, your fame would rival sun and moon, and not even Yi Yin or the Duke of Zhou could surpass you."

sentences.zh: 」卓曰：「吾亦悟之，卿言有意！」

translations.literal: Zhuo said: "I also have realized it; your words have meaning!"
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo answered, "I have begun to see that myself—your words carry weight!"

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之案：朗此對，但爲稱述卓功德，未相箴誨而已。

translations.literal: Your servant Song zhi notes: Lang's reply in this instance only extolled Zhuo's merit and virtue, and did not remonstrate or admonish.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi observes that Sima Lang's answer did nothing but praise Dong Zhuo's self-proclaimed virtues; it offered no real counsel.

sentences.zh: 了不自申釋，而卓便云「吾亦悟之，卿言有意」！

translations.literal: He did not personally explain himself at all, yet Zhuo then said "I also have realized it, your words have meaning"!
translations.idiomatic: Sima Lang never really cleared his own motives, yet Zhuo blithely replied that he "understood" and that Sima Lang had spoken "to the point."

sentences.zh: 客主之辭如爲不相酬塞也。〉

translations.literal: The language of guest and host seems as if they were not answering each other to closure.
translations.idiomatic: The exchange reads like two people talking past one another.

sentences.zh: 朗知卓必亡，恐見留，即散財物以賂遺卓用事者，求歸鄉里。

translations.literal: Lang knew Zhuo would surely perish, feared being detained, immediately scattered goods and treasures to bribe Zhuo's powerful attendants, sought to return to his village home.
translations.idiomatic: Certain Dong Zhuo was doomed and afraid of being held hostage, Sima Lang lavished bribes on the tyrant's favorites and won permission to take his kin back to Henei.

sentences.zh: 到謂父老曰；

translations.literal: When he arrived he said to the village elders:
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived he addressed the elders of the community:

sentences.zh: 「董卓悖逆，爲天下所讎，此忠臣義士奮發之時也。

translations.literal: "Dong Zhuo is perverse and rebellious, hated by the All-under-Heaven; this is the time for loyal ministers and righteous knights to rouse themselves."
translations.idiomatic: "Dong Zhuo flouts every moral law; the whole empire execrates him. This is the hour for loyal officers and men of honor to rise."

sentences.zh: 郡與京都境壤相接，洛東有成皋，北界大河，天下興義兵者若未得進，其勢必停於此。

translations.literal: The commandery borders the capital region; east of Luo is Chenggao, north borders the great river; those who raise righteous troops under Heaven, if they have not yet been able to advance, their momentum is sure to halt here.
translations.idiomatic: Our commandery adjoins the heartland of the realm: Chenggao lies east of Luoyang, the Yellow River bounds us on the north. Any coalition marching in the emperor's name that cannot push farther west will stall on this ground."

sentences.zh: 此乃四分五裂戰爭之地，難以自安，不如及道路尚通，舉宗東到黎陽。

translations.literal: This then is a battleground torn four ways and split five ways; it is hard to secure oneself; it is better while the roads are still open to move the whole clan east to Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: It is country doomed to be carved by rival armies—a poor place to sit out a storm. Better, while the roads still run clear, to escort your whole lineage east to Liyang."

sentences.zh: 黎陽有營兵，趙威孫鄉里舊婚，爲監營謁者，統兵馬，足以爲主。

translations.literal: Liyang has encampment troops; Zhao Weisun of my village is an old marriage connection, is Overseer of the Camp and Ye-zhe, commands infantry and cavalry, and is sufficient to be master.
translations.idiomatic: Liyang holds government troops, and my townsmate Zhao Weisun, an old family connection by marriage, serves as the camp's attending secretary with soldiers under his command—enough to shield us if trouble comes."

sentences.zh: 若後有變，徐復觀望未晚也。

translations.literal: If afterward there are changes, slowly again watching and waiting will not be late."
translations.idiomatic: Should new dangers appear later, we can still judge the moment—there will be time enough to reconsider."

sentences.zh: 」父老戀舊，莫有從者，惟同縣趙咨，將家屬俱與朗往焉。

translations.literal: The village elders were attached to their old places; none followed; only Zhao Zi of the same county, leading family dependents, together with Lang went.
translations.idiomatic: The elders clung to their homesteads and refused to stir; only his fellow townsman Zhao Zi moved his household alongside Sima Lang's.

sentences.zh: 後數月，關東諸州郡起兵，眾數十萬，皆集滎陽及河内。

translations.literal: After several months, the various prefectures and commanderies east of the pass raised troops; their masses were several hundred thousand, all gathering at Xingyang and Henei.
translations.idiomatic: A few months later the eastern allies rose by the hundred thousand, massing at Xingyang and inside Henei.

sentences.zh: 諸將不能相一，縱兵鈔略，民人死者且半。

translations.literal: The various generals could not unify; they released troops to plunder; among the common people who died were nearly half.
translations.idiomatic: Their commanders could not act as one and let their men pillage until nearly half the population perished.

sentences.zh: 久之，關東兵散，太祖與呂布相持於濮陽，朗乃將家還溫。

translations.literal: After a long time the armies east of the pass scattered; the Grand Progenitor and Lu Bu faced each other at Puyang; Lang then led the family back to Wen.
translations.idiomatic: When at length those armies melted away, Cao Cao and Lu Bu were locked in stalemate at Puyang, and Sima Lang brought his people home to Wen.

sentences.zh: 時歲大饑，人相食，朗收恤宗族，教訓諸弟，不爲衰世解業。

translations.literal: At the time the year had great famine; people ate each other; Lang gathered and comforted the clan, instructed the various younger brothers, and did not slacken studies because of a declining age.
translations.idiomatic: Famine stalked the land—men fed on one another—yet Sima Lang fed his kinsmen, schooled his younger brothers, and refused to let the collapse of the times excuse them from learning.

sentences.zh: 年二十二，太祖辟爲司空掾屬，除成皋令，以病去，復爲堂陽長。

translations.literal: At age twenty-two the Grand Progenitor summoned him as a clerk under the Director of Works, appointed magistrate of Chenggao; because of illness he departed, again became chief of Tangyang.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-two Cao Cao appointed him to the secretariat of the director of works, then magistrate of Chenggao; ill health forced him to resign, but he returned to office as chief of Tangyang.

sentences.zh: 其治務寬惠，不行鞭杖，而民不犯禁。

translations.literal: In his governance he stressed lenience and kindness; he did not apply whip or staff, yet the people did not violate prohibitions.
translations.idiomatic: His rule favored mercy over severity—he never lifted rod or lash—yet his subjects respected the law.

sentences.zh: 先時，民有徙充都内者，後縣調當作船，徙民恐其不辦，乃相率私還助之，其見愛如此。

translations.literal: Formerly, commoners had been moved to fill the capital interior; afterward the county was requisitioned to build boats; the moved commoners feared they could not finish; they mutually led one another privately to return and assist; he was loved like this.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, peasants had been relocated into the inner capital district. When the county was later ordered to build warships, those deportees feared the burden would go unfinished and quietly came back in a body to help build them—such was the devotion he inspired.

sentences.zh: 遷元城令，入爲丞相主簿。

translations.literal: He was transferred magistrate of Yuancheng, entered as chief clerk to the chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to magistrate of Yuancheng, then recalled to serve as chief clerk of the chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 朗以爲天下土崩之勢，由秦滅五等之制，而郡國無蒐狩習戰之備故也。

translations.literal: Lang thought that the situation of the empire's collapse was due to Qin having destroyed the five-ranks system, and commanderies and kingdoms lacking preparations for hunt-exercises and warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Lang argued that the realm's fragmentation stemmed from Qin's abolition of the feudal ranks, which left the commanderies without the old seasonal drills that had kept them battle-ready.

sentences.zh: 今雖五等未可復行，可令州郡並置兵，外備四夷，内威不軌，於策爲長。

translations.literal: Now though the five ranks cannot yet be restored, it is permissible to order commanderies and prefectures simultaneously to station troops—outwardly to prepare against the four barbarians, inwardly to awe those not keeping to the track—in policy this is the longest course.
translations.idiomatic: The five orders could not instantly be revived, he admitted, but every commandery should maintain a local militia—outwardly to garrison against border peoples, inwardly to cow local strongmen; that was the soundest long-term design.

sentences.zh: 又以爲宜復井田。

translations.literal: He again thought it fitting to restore the well-field system.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged revival of the well-field pattern of land tenure.

sentences.zh: 往者以民各有累世之業，難中奪之，是以至今。

translations.literal: Formerly because the people each had hereditary estates, it was difficult in the middle to strip them away; therefore down to the present it has been so.
translations.idiomatic: In earlier times families held land across generations, making resurvey and confiscation politically impossible, which was why reform had stalled.

sentences.zh: 今承大亂之後，民人分散，土業無主，皆爲公田，宜及此時復之。

translations.literal: Now following the great chaos afterward, the people are scattered, land and estates have no masters, all have become public fields—it is fitting to take this moment and restore it.
translations.idiomatic: The great upheaval had uprooted millions and left vast tracts without clear owners—ideal moment, he said, to restore public allocation of fields.

sentences.zh: 議雖未施行，然州郡领兵，朗本意也。

translations.literal: Though the deliberation was not put into practice, yet commanderies and prefectures leading troops was Lang's original meaning.
translations.idiomatic: The court never adopted the full program, yet the system of regional levies that later emerged matched Sima Lang's intent.

sentences.zh: 遷兗州刺史，政化大行，百姓稱之。

translations.literal: He was transferred Inspector of Yanzhou; administrative transformation was broadly carried out; the common people praised him.
translations.idiomatic: As inspector of Yanzhou he spread administrative reform and won universal praise.

sentences.zh: 雖在軍旅，常粗衣恶食，俭以率下。

translations.literal: Though in the army he constantly wore coarse clothes and ate bad food, frugal to lead those below.
translations.idiomatic: Even on campaign he dressed in rough cloth, ate plain fare, and set the example of austerity for his men.

sentences.zh: 雅好人伦典籍，鄉人李觌等盛得名誉，朗常显贬下之；

translations.literal: He elegantly loved human relations texts and classics; his fellow villagers Li Gu and others had flourishing reputations; Lang constantly openly demoted and placed them low;
translations.idiomatic: He cultivated a taste for works on moral character, and when neighbors such as Li Gu enjoyed inflated reputations, Sima Lang was quick to puncture their pretensions in public;

sentences.zh: 後觌等敗，時人服焉。

translations.literal: Later Gu and others were defeated; people of the time admired him.
translations.idiomatic: when those same men later fell in scandal, contemporaries conceded he had seen through them.

sentences.zh: 锺繇、王粲著论云：「非圣人不能致太平。

translations.literal: Zhong Yao and Wang Can authored a treatise saying: "If not a sage one cannot bring about grand peace."
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yao and Wang Can had published a thesis: "Only a sage can achieve universal tranquility."

sentences.zh: 」朗以爲「伊、颜之徒雖非圣人，使得數世相承，太平可致」。

translations.literal: Lang thought that "disciples of Yi and Yan though not sages, if made to succeed for generations, grand peace can be brought about."
translations.idiomatic: Sima Lang countered that "men in the mold of Yi Yin and Yan Hui, though short of sagehood, could still deliver lasting peace if succession held steady for generations."

sentences.zh: 〈魏書曰：文帝善朗论，命秘書录其文。

translations.literal: The Wei shu says: Emperor Wen approved Lang's treatise and ordered the secretariat to record his text.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei shu adds that Cao Pi admired his argument and had the palace secretariat copy it into the archives.

sentences.zh: 孫盛曰：繇既失之，朗亦未爲得也。

translations.literal: Sun Sheng says: Yao also missed the mark, and Lang too was not correct.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng retorts that Zhong Yao was wrong—and Sima Lang no less so.

sentences.zh: 昔「汤舉伊尹，而不仁者远矣」。

translations.literal: Formerly "Tang raised Yi Yin, and the un-virtuous departed far away."
translations.idiomatic: The old text says, "When Tang lifted up Yi Yin, the cruel vanished far away."

sentences.zh: 易稱「颜氏之子，其殆庶幾乎！

translations.literal: The Yi says "The son of Yan's clan—perhaps he was almost there!"
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes praises "Yan Hui's sort" as coming nearest perfection.

sentences.zh: 有不善未尝不知，知之未尝復行」。

translations.literal: "When he does wrong he never fails to know it; having known it, he never again commits the error."
translations.idiomatic: The Changes add, "He never fails to notice his own faults; once he sees them, he never repeats them."

sentences.zh: 由此而言，圣人之與大賢，行藏道一，舒卷斯同，御世垂風，理無降異；

translations.literal: From this speaking, as between a sage and a great worthy, in advancing and withdrawing the Way is one, in spreading and rolling up thus the same, in ruling the age and bequeathing custom, in principle there is no lowering of difference;
translations.idiomatic: From this it follows that sage and near-sage walk the same path of service or withdrawal, expand or contract by the same rule, and set the tone for their age without a real gulf in principle;

sentences.zh: 升泰之美，豈俟积世哉？

translations.literal: the beauty of ascending to grand peace—how could it wait for accumulated generations?
translations.idiomatic: the glory of bringing the world to perfect calm need not wait for many lifetimes to pile up.

sentences.zh: 「善人爲邦百年，亦可以胜残去杀」。

translations.literal: "If a good man governs the state for a hundred years, he can overcome cruelty and remove killing."
translations.idiomatic: The Analects promise that "if a good man held the state for a century, he could end cruelty and do away with executions."

sentences.zh: 又曰「不践迹，亦不入于室」。

translations.literal: It also says: "He does not tread in others' footsteps, yet neither does he enter the inner chamber."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius also says, "Without treading in another's footprints, one still may not reach the inner sanctum."

sentences.zh: 數世之论，其在斯乎！

translations.literal: The thesis of "several generations"—is it not here!
translations.idiomatic: So much for the argument that peace must wait on many reigns!

sentences.zh: 方之大賢，固有間矣。〉

translations.literal: Compared to a great worthy, indeed there is a distance.〉
translations.idiomatic: Measured against a true paragon, Sima Lang still stood a step below.〉

sentences.zh: 初朗所與俱徙趙咨，官至太常，爲世好士。

translations.literal: At first Zhao Zi, who together with Lang had moved east, reached the office of Minister of Ceremonies and was for his generation a fine lover of scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zi, who had fled east with Sima Lang, rose to minister of rituals and was celebrated in his day as a patron of learning.

sentences.zh: 〈咨字君初。

translations.literal: Zi's courtesy name was Junchu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zi's courtesy name was Junchu.

sentences.zh: 子酆字子，晉骠骑將軍，封東平陵公。

translations.literal: His son Feng, courtesy name Zi, was General of Agile Cavalry in Jin and was enfeoffed Duke of Dongpingling.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhao Feng—style Zi—became Jin's general of agile cavalry and received the ducal title of Dongpingling.

sentences.zh: 並見百官名

translations.literal: Both are seen in the Register of Officials.
translations.idiomatic: Both men are listed in the roster of official titles.

translations.literal: (Record)
translations.idiomatic: (from the monograph)

sentences.zh: 梁習字子虞，陳郡柘人也，爲郡纲纪。

translations.literal: Liang Xi, courtesy name Ziyu, was a native of Zhe in the Principality of Chen, and served as chief clerk of his commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Xi, style Ziyu, came from Zhe in Chen commandery and had risen to chief clerk of the local administration.

sentences.zh: 太祖爲司空，辟召爲漳長，累轉乘氏、海西、下邳令，所在有治名。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor was Director of Works, he summoned Xi and appointed him chief of Zhang, and he successively transferred to be magistrate of Chengshi, Haixi, and Xiapi; wherever he went he had a reputation for good order.
translations.idiomatic: While Cao Cao held the directorship of works, he called Liang Xi to office as magistrate of Zhang, then rotated him through Chengshi, Haixi, and Xiapi, each time leaving a record of capable rule.

sentences.zh: 還爲西曹令史，遷爲屬。

translations.literal: He returned as clerk secretary of the West Bureau and was promoted to a staff aide.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the western bureau as recording secretary and soon promoted into the chancellor's staff corps.

sentences.zh: 並土新附，習以别部司馬领並州刺史。

translations.literal: Bingzhou had newly submitted; Xi as major of a separate column concurrently acted as Inspector of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Bingzhou first came over, Liang Xi, though only a major commanding a detached column, was given concurrent charge as inspector of the province.

sentences.zh: 時承高幹荒亂之餘，胡狄在界，張雄跋扈，吏民亡叛，入其部落；

translations.literal: At the time, following the aftermath of Gao Gan's wasteland chaos, Hu and Di were on the borders, Zhang Xiong ran rampant, clerks and commoners fled in rebellion and entered their tribal camps;
translations.idiomatic: The province still reeled from Gao Gan's rebellion: Xiongnu and Di pressed the frontier, Zhang Xiong bullied the countryside, and officials and peasants alike deserted into the steppe camps;

sentences.zh: 兵家拥眾，作爲寇害，更相扇動，往往釭跱。

translations.literal: military households hugging their followings acted as bandits doing harm, mutually fanned and stirred one another, and everywhere stood like rivets in opposition.
translations.idiomatic: garrison families with private armies turned to pillage, egged one another on, and formed hostile pockets that would not yield.

sentences.zh: 習到官，诱谕招纳，皆礼召其豪右，稍稍荐舉，使詣幕府；

translations.literal: When Xi arrived at his post, he enticed and instructed them to recruit and accept submission, ritually summoned their local magnates, gradually recommended them, and had them come to headquarters;
translations.idiomatic: Liang Xi set about coaxing leaders back to allegiance: he summoned the great houses with courtesy, advanced their names step by step, and brought them in to serve at headquarters;

sentences.zh: 豪右已尽，乃次发諸丁强以爲義從；

translations.literal: when the magnates were exhausted, he next mobilized the adult males among the commoners to serve as volunteer auxiliaries;
translations.idiomatic: once the notables were exhausted, he drafted able-bodied freemen as sworn militia;

sentences.zh: 又因大軍出征，分请以爲勇力。

translations.literal: furthermore, whenever the main host marched, he detached parties of them to serve as shock troops.
translations.idiomatic: whenever the field army marched, he detached contingents of those same men as assault troops.

sentences.zh: 吏兵已去之後，稍移其家，前後送鄴，凡數萬口；

translations.literal: After the clerks and soldiers had departed, he gradually moved their families forward and rearward to Ye, in all several tens of thousands of persons;
translations.idiomatic: After the regular troops left, he shifted their dependents in waves to Ye until tens of thousands of mouths had been resettled;

sentences.zh: 其不從命者，興兵致讨，斩首千數，降附者萬计。

translations.literal: those who did not obey orders he attacked with arms, beheading by the thousand; those who surrendered and attached were counted in the ten thousands.
translations.idiomatic: recalcitrants he struck down by the thousand; those who submitted he counted by the myriad.

sentences.zh: 单于恭顺，名王稽颡，部曲服事供职，同於编户。

translations.literal: The Shanyu was respectful and submissive, the titled kings knocked their foreheads on the ground, and tribal followings performed corvée duties like registered commoners.
translations.idiomatic: The chanyu bowed in submission, the great chiefs kowtowed, and tribal followings paid labor and grain levies on the same schedule as ordinary households.

sentences.zh: 邊境肅清，百姓布野，勤勸农桑，令行禁止。

translations.literal: The border was cleared, the common people spread across the fields, he diligently urged farming and sericulture, and orders were executed and prohibitions enforced.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier grew quiet, farmers returned to the open country, he pushed plough and loom with equal vigor, and his commands were obeyed to the letter.

sentences.zh: 贡達名士，咸显於世，语在《常林傳》。

translations.literal: For tribute students and eminent scholars, all became prominent in their generation; the account is in the "Biography of Chang Lin."
translations.idiomatic: Recommended talents and noted scholars alike rose to fame—their stories are told in the biography of Chang Lin.

sentences.zh: 初，济阴王思與習俱爲西曹令史。

translations.literal: At first Wang Si of Jiyin together with Xi had both been clerks of the West Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Si of Jiyin had begun his career alongside Liang Xi as a western-bureau secretary.

sentences.zh: 思因直日白事，失太祖指。

translations.literal: Si, because on the day of his watch he reported affairs, missed the Grand Progenitor's intention.
translations.idiomatic: One day when it was Wang Si's turn on duty, he briefed Cao Cao and badly misread what the chancellor wanted.

sentences.zh: 太祖大怒，教召主者，將加重辟。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor was greatly angry, ordered the responsible official summoned, and was about to impose capital punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao flew into a rage, demanded the responsible registrar, and prepared to execute him.

sentences.zh: 時思近出，習代往對，已被收執矣，思乃驰還，自陳己罪，罪应受死。

translations.literal: At the time Si had gone out nearby; Xi went in his place to answer, already had been seized and arrested; Si then galloped back, personally declared his own crime, and said the crime deserved death.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Si had stepped out on an errand; Liang Xi went to answer for him and was seized in his stead. Wang Si raced back, confessed his own fault, and declared himself worthy of death.

sentences.zh: 太祖叹習之不言，思之识分，曰：「何意吾軍中有二義士乎？」

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor sighed at Xi's not speaking out and Si's knowing his allotted share, and said: "Who would have thought my army held two righteous knights?"
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao marveled that Liang Xi had volunteered silence while Wang Si owned his duty, and exclaimed, "Could I really command two such men of honor?"

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之以爲習與王思，同寮而已，親非骨肉，義非刎颈，而以身代思，受不测之祸。

translations.literal: Your servant Song zhi thinks: Xi and Wang Si were only colleagues in the same office; kin was not flesh and bone, righteousness was not cut-throat friendship, yet he used his body to replace Si and received immeasurable disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi comments that Liang Xi and Wang Si were mere office mates—neither blood brothers nor sworn companions—yet Liang stepped forward to die in Wang's place and risked an unpredictable fate.

sentences.zh: 以之爲義，無乃乖先哲之雅旨乎！

translations.literal: To call this "righteousness"—is it not contrary to the refined meaning of the former sages!
translations.idiomatic: To label that "heroic sacrifice" seems to trample the measured teaching of the ancients!

sentences.zh: 史遷云「死有重於太山，有轻於鸿毛」，故君子不爲苟存，不爲苟亡。

translations.literal: Sima Qian said, "Death may be heavier than Mount Tai or lighter than a wild goose's down"; therefore the gentleman does not cling to life at random, nor throw life away at random.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Qian wrote that some deaths weigh more than Mount Tai and others less than a feather; the noble man neither clings to life without cause nor casts it away without cause.

sentences.zh: 若使思不引分，主不加恕，則所謂自經於沟渎而莫之知也。

translations.literal: If it had made Si not take his allotted share and the lord not add forgiveness, then what is called "hanging oneself in a ditch with none to know" would apply.
translations.idiomatic: Had Wang Si refused to accept blame and his lord refused mercy, he would have ended as "a corpse in a ditch that nobody notices."

sentences.zh: 習之死義者，豈其然哉！〉

translations.literal: That Xi "died for righteousness"—can it really be so!〉
translations.idiomatic: Calling Liang Xi's act "dying for righteousness" strains credulity.〉

sentences.zh: 後同時擢爲刺史，思领豫州。

translations.literal: Later they were at the same time promoted to inspectors; Si led Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later both men were raised to provincial inspector; Wang Si received Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 思亦能吏，然苛碎無大體，官至九卿，封列侯。

translations.literal: Si was also a capable clerk, yet was harsh and fragmented without large substance; his office reached the Nine Ministers and he was enfeoffed a full marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Si remained a competent bureaucrat, but petty and fussy, never seeing the larger picture; he rose to one of the nine ministers and a full marquisate.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略苛吏傳》曰：思與薛悌、郤嘉俱從微起，官位略等。

translations.literal: The Wei lue "Biography of Harsh Officials" says: Si together with Xue Ti and Xi Jia all rose from low beginnings, their official positions roughly equal.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei lue chapter on harsh magistrates notes that Wang Si, Xue Ti, and Xi Jia all climbed from humble posts to comparable rank.

sentences.zh: 三人中，悌差挟儒术，所在名爲間省。

translations.literal: Among the three, Ti slightly embraced Confucian arts; where he went was called relaxed and efficient.
translations.idiomatic: Of the three, Xue Ti alone leaned on Confucian learning and earned a reputation for lean, efficient government.

sentences.zh: 嘉與思事行相似。

translations.literal: Jia and Si in affairs and conduct were similar.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jia and Wang Si governed in much the same fashion.

sentences.zh: 文帝詔曰：「薛悌驳吏，王思、郤嘉纯吏也，各赐關内侯，以报其勤。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen's edict said: "Xue Ti is a disputatious clerk; Wang Si and Xi Jia are pure clerks; each is granted Neighbourhood Marquis to repay their diligence."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi's rescript read: "Xue Ti is the argumentative clerk; Wang Si and Xi Jia are the blunt, literal-minded ones—grant each a neighborhood marquisate for their long service."

sentences.zh: 」思爲人雖烦碎，而晓练文書，敬賢礼士，倾意形勢，亦以是显名。

translations.literal: Though Si as a person was bothersome and fragmented, yet he was expert in documents, respected worthies and treated knights courteously, inclined to power and situation, and also therefore had a manifest name.
translations.idiomatic: Picky though he was, Wang Si knew paperwork inside out, cultivated men of talent, and curried favor with the mighty, which kept his name in circulation.

sentences.zh: 正始中，爲大司农，年老目瞑，瞋怒無度，下吏嗷然不知何据。

translations.literal: In the Zhengshi period he was Minister of Agriculture; in old age his eyes went blind, his rages knew no limit, and subordinate officials wailed without knowing on what grounds.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhengshi reign he became minister of agriculture; blindness and ungovernable temper left his staff guessing what had set him off.

sentences.zh: 性少信，時有吏父病笃，近在外舍，自白求假。

translations.literal: His nature had little trust; at the time a clerk's father was gravely ill in quarters nearby, and he personally explained seeking leave.
translations.idiomatic: He trusted no one. Once a clerk's father lay dying in an outbuilding, and the son asked leave to attend him.

sentences.zh: 思疑其不實，发怒曰：「世有思妇病母者，豈此謂乎！

translations.literal: Si suspected it was not true and angrily said: "In the world are there cases of 'the wife in labor and the mother ill'—is this what is meant!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Si decided it was a lie and shouted, "People invent dead wives and dying mothers every day—is this another of those stories!"

sentences.zh: 」遂不與假。

translations.literal: Thereupon he did not grant leave.
translations.idiomatic: He refused the request.

sentences.zh: 吏父明日死，思無恨意。

translations.literal: The clerk's father died the next day; Si had no regretful thought.
translations.idiomatic: The father died the following morning; Wang Si felt not the slightest remorse.

sentences.zh: 其爲刻薄类如此。

translations.literal: His being harsh and mean was of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the meanness of his temper.

sentences.zh: 思又性急，尝執笔作書，蝇集笔端，驱去復来，如是再三。

translations.literal: Also Si's nature was hasty; once while grasping a brush to write a letter, flies swarmed on the brush tip; driven off they returned again, thus three times.
translations.idiomatic: He was also irascible: once, while drafting a letter, flies settled on his brush; he brushed them off three times and they returned.

sentences.zh: 思恚怒，自起逐蝇不能得，還取笔掷地，蹋坏之。

translations.literal: Si grew furious, himself rose to chase the flies but could not catch them, returned, took the brush, threw it on the ground, and trampled and broke it.
translations.idiomatic: He sprang up to swat them, failed, snatched up the brush, hurled it down, and stamped it to splinters.

sentences.zh: 時有丹陽施畏、鲁郡倪顗、南陽胡業亦爲刺史、郡守，時人謂之苛暴。

translations.literal: At the time Shi Wei of Danyang, Ni Yi of Lu commandery, and Hu Ye of Nanyang also were inspectors and governors; people of the time called them harsh and violent.
translations.idiomatic: Around the same time Shi Wei in Danyang, Ni Yi in Lu, and Hu Ye in Nanyang held provincial posts and were branded cruel magistrates.

sentences.zh: ◎又有高陽刘类，歷位宰守，苛慝尤其，以善修人事，不废於世。

translations.literal: ◎ Moreover there was Liu Lei of Gaoyang, who passed through positions as governor; his harsh wickedness was especially extreme, yet because he was good at cultivating human affairs he was not discarded by the age.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Liu Lei of Gaoyang, whose successive prefectures were models of viciousness; because he flattered the right people, he nevertheless survived politically.

sentences.zh: 嘉平中，爲弘农太守。

translations.literal: In the Jiaping period he was Administrator of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: During Jiaping he became prefect of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 吏二百餘人，不與休假，专使爲不急。

translations.literal: More than two hundred clerks were denied holidays and were exclusively set to trivial tasks.
translations.idiomatic: He kept over two hundred clerks on duty without leave and set them to pointless busywork.

sentences.zh: 过無轻重，辄捽其头，又亂杖挝之，牵出復入，如是數四。

translations.literal: For faults without regard to light or heavy, he always seized their heads and also chaotically beat them with sticks, dragging them out and bringing them back in, thus four times.
translations.idiomatic: Petty or serious, every slip earned a beating: he would grab a man by the hair, club him at random, drag him out and in again—four rounds of the same abuse.

sentences.zh: 乃使人掘地求钱，所在市里，皆有孔穴。

translations.literal: He also had people dig the ground seeking money; wherever in market and hamlet, all had holes.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered trenches dug through markets and lanes in a lunatic search for buried coin until the town was honeycombed with pits.

sentences.zh: 又外讬简省，每出行，陽敕督邮不得使官屬曲修礼敬，而阴识不来者，辄发怒中伤之。

translations.literal: Also outwardly he claimed simplicity and economy; every time he went out he openly ordered the supervising clerk not to allow official subordinates to bend in performing ritual courtesy, but secretly marked those who did not come, then grew angry and slandered them.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly he preached austerity: whenever he toured the district he publicly forbade clerks to kneel in greeting, then secretly noted who stayed away and later punished them for disrespect.

sentences.zh: 性又少信，每遣大吏出，辄使小吏随覆察之，白日常自於墙壁間闚闪，夜使幹廉察諸曹，復以幹不足信，又遣铃下及奴婢使轉相检验。

translations.literal: His nature again had little trust; every time he dispatched a senior clerk he always had a junior clerk follow to spy and inspect; in broad daylight he personally peeped and flashed between walls; at night he had runners secretly observe the various bureaus; again because the runners were not enough to be trusted, he also dispatched bell-standers and slave girls to take turns verifying.
translations.idiomatic: He trusted no subordinate: senior aides went out shadowed by juniors, he himself spied from alley corners by day, sent night patrols to watch each office, and still posted bell-guards and household slaves to cross-check one another.

sentences.zh: 尝案行，宿止民家。

translations.literal: Once while on inspection rounds he lodged in a commoner's house.
translations.idiomatic: On one inspection tour he billeted himself in a peasant cottage.

sentences.zh: 民家二狗逐猪，猪惊走，头插栅間，号呼良久。

translations.literal: The house's two dogs chased a pig; the pig bolted in alarm, its head stuck between fence slats, and squealed for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Two farm dogs cornered a pig; the beast panicked, wedged its head in the fence rails, and squealed endlessly.

sentences.zh: 类以爲外之吏擅共饮食，不復徵察，便使伍百曳五官掾孫弼入，顿头责之。

translations.literal: Lei thought it was outside clerks privately feasting together; he did not again investigate, but had the company of five hundred drag in the senior clerk Sun Bi, knock his head, and rebuke him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lei assumed his staff were feasting without permission. Without looking further, he had runners haul in chief clerk Sun Bi, beat his head on the floor, and berate him.

sentences.zh: 弼以實對，类自愧不详，因讬問以他事。

translations.literal: Bi answered with the facts; Lei himself was ashamed at not having examined in detail, and therefore used other affairs as a pretext to question.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Bi told the truth; mortified at his own rashness, Liu Lei changed the subject to save face.

sentences.zh: 民尹昌，年垂百歲，聞类出行，當經过，謂其兒曰：「扶我迎府君，我欲陳恩。

translations.literal: The commoner Yin Chang, his years nearing a hundred, heard Lei was on the road and would pass by, and said to his son: "Support me to welcome the prefect; I wish to declare kindness."
translations.idiomatic: A centenarian named Yin Chang heard the prefect was coming and told his son, "Help me out to the road—I want to thank him for his kindness."

sentences.zh: 」兒扶昌在道左，类望見，呵其兒曰：「用是死人，使来見我。

translations.literal: The son supported Chang on the left of the road; Lei saw them from afar and shouted at the son: "What use is this dead man—making him come to see me!"
translations.idiomatic: The old man waited by the roadside; Liu Lei spotted him and yelled at the son, "Why drag that corpse out to block my way!"

sentences.zh: 」其视人無礼，皆此类也。

translations.literal: His viewing people without ritual was all of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: His contempt for ordinary folk was habitual.

sentences.zh: 舊俗，民谤官長者有三不肯，謂遷、免與死也。

translations.literal: By old custom, when commoners slandered a long official there were three things they were unwilling to have happen, meaning transfer, dismissal, and death.
translations.idiomatic: Folk wisdom held that people might rail at a magistrate yet still dread three outcomes for him—transfer, dismissal, or death.

sentences.zh: 类在弘农，吏民患之，乃题其門曰：「刘府君有三不肯。

translations.literal: When Lei was in Hongnong, clerks and commoners suffered him and therefore inscribed his gate: "Prefect Liu has three things he is unwilling to do."
translations.idiomatic: Under Liu Lei's rule the people suffered so badly they chalked on his gate, "Our Prefect Liu refuses all three of those mercies."

sentences.zh: 」类雖聞之，猶不能自改。

translations.literal: Though Lei heard it, still he could not reform himself.
translations.idiomatic: He saw the graffito and still could not mend his ways.

sentences.zh: 其後安東將軍司馬文王西征，路經弘农，弘农人告类荒耄不任宰郡，乃召入爲五官中郎將。〉

translations.literal: Afterward when General Who Guards the East Sima Zhao campaigned west and his route passed Hongnong, the people of Hongnong reported that Lei was senile and unfit to govern a commandery; therefore he was summoned in as Central Gentleman of the Household.〉
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Sima Zhao marched west through Hongnong, the locals petitioned that Liu Lei was too senile to govern; he was recalled to a sinceure as central gentleman of the household.〉

sentences.zh: 張旣字德容，馮翊高陵人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Ji, courtesy name Derong, was a native of Gaoling in Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji, style Derong, was a man of Gaoling in the Fengyi region.

sentences.zh: 年十六，為郡小吏。

translations.literal: At age sixteen he was a petty clerk of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he was already a junior clerk in the county office.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：旣世單家富，為人有容儀。

translations.literal: The Wei lue says: For generations Ji's family had been a single-household line yet was wealthy; as a person he had bearing and appearance.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei lue records that although Zhang Ji's clan was small it was rich, and he himself carried himself with polish.

sentences.zh: 少小工書疏，為郡門下小吏，而家富。

translations.literal: From youth he was skilled at letters and memoranda; he was a petty clerk under the commandery gate, yet his family was wealthy.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a gate clerk he excelled at brush correspondence, while his family's wealth set him apart from other petty functionaries.

sentences.zh: 自惟門寒，念無以自達，乃常畜好刀筆及版奏，伺諸大吏有乏者輒給與，以是見識焉。〉

translations.literal: He alone thought his gate was cold and worried there was no means to make himself known; therefore he constantly stored fine knives, brushes, and wooden tablets, watched for various great clerks who lacked supplies and always supplied them, and by this means was noticed.〉
translations.idiomatic: Fearing his modest pedigree would block promotion, he stocked fine pens, ink knives, and wooden slips and quietly supplied any senior clerk who ran short—thus he came to be noticed.〉

sentences.zh: 後歷右職，舉孝廉，不行。

translations.literal: Later he passed through senior posts, was recommended Filial and Incorrupt, but did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through weightier posts, earned nomination as filial and incorrupt, yet declined appointment.

sentences.zh: 太祖為司空，辟，未至，舉茂才，除新豐令，治為三輔第一。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor was Director of Works, he summoned him; before he arrived he was recommended Outstanding Talent, appointed magistrate of Xinfeng, and his governance was first in the Three Supports.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao summoned him to the directorate of works; before he reported, another board named him for "outstanding talent," and as magistrate of Xinfeng he ranked first among the capital counties.

sentences.zh: 袁尚拒太祖於黎陽，遣所置河東太守郭援、並州刺史高幹及匈奴單于取平陽，發使西與關中諸將合從。

translations.literal: Yuan Shao's son Shang resisted the Grand Progenitor at Liyang; he dispatched his appointed Administrator of Hedong Guo Yuan, Inspector of Bingzhou Gao Gan, and the Xiongnu Shanyu to seize Pingyang, and sent envoys west to join the pass generals in a vertical alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shang held Cao Cao at Liyang and sent his Hedong prefect Guo Yuan, Bingzhou inspector Gao Gan, and the Xiongnu chanyu to seize Pingyang while couriers negotiated a western alliance with the generals inside the passes.

sentences.zh: 司隷校尉鍾繇遣旣說將軍馬騰等，旣為言利害，騰等從之。

translations.literal: The Colonel Director of Retainers Zhong Yao dispatched Ji to persuade Generals Ma Teng and others; Ji for them spoke profit and harm, and Teng and others followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Colonel of the metropolitan guard Zhong Yao sent Zhang Ji to sway Ma Teng and the other Liangzhou generals; Zhang Ji laid out the stakes until they agreed to cooperate.

sentences.zh: 騰遣子超將兵萬餘人，與繇會擊幹、援，大破之，斬援首。

translations.literal: Teng dispatched his son Chao leading more than ten thousand troops to join Yao in striking Gan and Yuan; they greatly defeated them and beheaded Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Teng released Ma Chao with ten thousand horse to join Zhong Yao; together they shattered Gao Gan and Guo Yuan and sent Guo Yuan's head to the camp.

sentences.zh: 幹及單于皆降。

translations.literal: Gan and the Shanyu both surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gan and the chanyu both capitulated.

sentences.zh: 其後幹復舉並州反。

translations.literal: Afterward Gan again raised Bingzhou in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gan later rebelled again and seized Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 河內張晟衆萬餘人無所屬，冦崤、澠閒，河東衞固、弘農張琰各起兵以應之。

translations.literal: Zhang Sheng of Henei with a following of more than ten thousand belonged to no master, raided between Xiao and Mian; Wei Gu of Hedong and Zhang Yan of Hongnong each raised troops to respond to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Sheng of Henei led ten thousand unattached bandits between Xiao and Mian; Wei Gu in Hedong and Zhang Yan in Hongnong rose in support.

sentences.zh: 太祖以旣為議郎，參繇軍事，使西徵諸將馬騰等，皆引兵會擊晟等，破之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor made Ji Consultant Counselor, attached him to Yao's military affairs, had him go west to summon Generals Ma Teng and others, all of whom led troops to join in striking Sheng and others, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao named Zhang Ji a consultant cadre on Zhong Yao's staff, sent him west to rally Ma Teng, and the combined force crushed Zhang Sheng.

sentences.zh: 斬琰、固首，幹奔荊州。

translations.literal: They beheaded Yan and Gu's heads; Gan fled to Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yan and Wei Gu fell; Gao Gan bolted for Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 封旣武始亭侯。

translations.literal: Ji was enfeoffed Marquis of Wushi Village.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji received the village marquisate of Wushi.

sentences.zh: 太祖將征荊州，而騰等分據關中。

translations.literal: At this time the Grand Progenitor was about to campaign against Jingzhou, while Teng and others separately held Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Just as Cao Cao prepared to strike south, Ma Teng and the western lords still partitioned Guanzhong among themselves.

sentences.zh: 太祖復遣旣喻騰等，令釋部曲求還。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor again dispatched Ji to instruct Teng and others, ordering them to disband their private armies and seek to return.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao sent Zhang Ji again to urge Ma Teng to dissolve his host and come in.

sentences.zh: 騰已許之而更猶豫，旣恐為變，乃移諸縣促儲偫，二千石郊迎。

translations.literal: Teng had already promised but still hesitated; Ji feared there would be a mutiny, therefore moved the various counties to hurry stores, and the two-thousand-bushel officials went to the suburbs to welcome.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Teng had given his word yet wavered; fearing a coup, Zhang Ji ordered every county to pile supplies and sent each two-thousand-bushel magistrate out to greet the court column.

sentences.zh: 騰不得已，發東。

translations.literal: Teng had no choice but to set out east.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, Ma Teng marched east toward the capital.

sentences.zh: 太祖表騰為衞尉，子超為將軍，統其衆。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor memorialized Teng as Commandant of the Guards and his son Chao as general, commanding his masses.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao had Ma Teng named commandant of the guards while Ma Chao took command of the tribal host.

sentences.zh: 後超反，旣從太祖破超於華陰，西定關右。

translations.literal: Later when Chao rebelled, Ji followed the Grand Progenitor in defeating Chao at Huayin and pacifying Guanxi to the west.
translations.idiomatic: After Ma Chao rose in revolt, Zhang Ji followed Cao Cao to crush him at Huayin and secure the western march.

sentences.zh: 以旣為京兆尹，招懷流民，興復縣邑，百姓懷之。

translations.literal: He made Ji Governor of the capital region, who summoned and comforted displaced people, restored counties and towns, and the common people cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji was then made governor of the capital district, where he resettled refugees, rebuilt townships, and won the people's affection.

sentences.zh: 魏國旣建，為尚書，出為雍州刺史。

translations.literal: When the Wei state was established, he became Minister of the Interior, went out as Inspector of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the duchy of Wei was founded he entered the ministry of the interior, then went out again as inspector of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 太祖謂旣曰：「還君本州，可謂衣繡晝行矣。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor said to Ji: "Returning you to your home province may be called wearing embroidered robes in broad daylight."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao told him, "Sending you home in silks by daylight is the ancient metaphor for honoring a man in his own country."

sentences.zh: 」從征張魯，別從散關入討叛氐，收其麥以給軍食。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Zhang Lu, separately entered from Sanguan to attack rebellious Di, gathered their wheat to supply the army's food.
translations.idiomatic: On the Zhang Lu expedition he led a column through Sanguan against mutinous Di tribes and seized their winter wheat for the commissary.

sentences.zh: 魯降，旣說太祖拔漢中民數萬戶以實長安及三輔。

translations.literal: When Lu surrendered, Ji persuaded the Grand Progenitor to relocate several tens of thousands of households of Hanzhong people to fill Chang'an and the Three Supports.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Lu capitulated, Zhang Ji convinced Cao Cao to move tens of thousands of Hanzhong families into Chang'an and the three capital counties.

sentences.zh: 其後與曹洪破吳蘭於下辯，又與夏侯淵討宋建，別攻臨洮、狄道，平之。

translations.literal: Afterward together with Cao Hong he defeated Wu Lan at Xiabian, and together with Xiahou Yuan attacked Song Jian, separately attacked Lintao and Didao, and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: He later joined Cao Hong in defeating Wu Lan at Xiabian and Xiahou Yuan in the campaign against Song Jian, himself clearing Lintao and Didao.

sentences.zh: 是時，太祖徙民以充河北，隴西、天水、南安民相恐動，擾擾不安，旣假三郡人為將吏者休課，使治屋宅，作水碓，民心遂安。

translations.literal: At this time the Grand Progenitor moved people to fill Hebei; the people of Longxi, Tianshui, and Nan'an mutually feared and stirred, disturbed and not at peace; Ji gave furloughs to the people of the three commanderies who served as generals and clerks, had them build houses and dwellings, construct water trip-hammers, and the people's hearts thereupon were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao shifted population north to fill Hebei, the western commanderies of Longxi, Tianshui, and Nan'an panicked; Zhang Ji exempted local officers from labor levies, set them to building houses and water-powered mills, and calm returned.

sentences.zh: 太祖將拔漢中守，恐劉備北取武都氐以逼關中，問旣。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor was about to withdraw the defense of Hanzhong, feared Liu Bei would take the Wudu Di to the north and press Guanzhong, and asked Ji.
translations.idiomatic: As Cao Cao prepared to pull his garrison out of Hanzhong, he worried Liu Bei might seize the Wudu Di tribesmen and thrust toward Guanzhong, and he turned to Zhang Ji for counsel.

sentences.zh: 旣曰：「可勸使北出就穀以避賊，前至者厚其寵賞，則先者知利，後必慕之。

translations.literal: Ji said: "One can urge them to go north to seek grain and avoid the bandits; for those who arrive first richly favor and reward them, then those in front will know profit and those behind will surely admire them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji replied, "Urge those tribes to march north for grain and to escape your retreating columns; reward handsomely whoever arrives first so others will rush to follow."

sentences.zh: 」太祖從其策，乃自到漢中引出諸軍，令旣之武都，徙氐五萬餘落出居扶風、天水界。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor followed his plan, thereupon personally went to Hanzhong to lead out the various armies, ordered Ji to go to Wudu, and moved more than fifty thousand Di households out to dwell on the border between Fufeng and Tianshui."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao adopted the plan, personally brought the field army out of Hanzhong, and sent Zhang Ji into Wudu to relocate over fifty thousand Di households to the Fufeng–Tianshui frontier."

sentences.zh: 〈《三輔決錄注》曰：旣為兒童，為郡功曹游殷察異之，引旣過家，旣敬諾。

translations.literal: The Sanfu jue lu zhu says: When Ji was a child, the merit assessor You Yin of the commandery marked him as unusual, led Ji past his home, and Ji respectfully assented.
translations.idiomatic: The Sanfu jue lu commentary records that in boyhood Zhang Ji caught the eye of the local merit clerk You Yin, who took him home—and the lad accepted the invitation with proper deference.

sentences.zh: 殷先歸，勑家具設賔饌。

translations.literal: Yin first returned, ordered his household fully to set out guest feasting.
translations.idiomatic: You Yin hurried ahead and told his wife to lay on a full banquet for an honored guest.

sentences.zh: 及旣至，殷妻笑曰：「君其悖乎！

translations.literal: When Ji arrived, Yin's wife laughed and said: "Husband, are you muddled!"
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Ji arrived, You Yin's wife laughed, "Have you lost your wits?"

sentences.zh: 張德容童昏小兒，何異客哉！

translations.literal: Zhang Derong is a dim-witted little boy—what difference from an ordinary visitor!"
translations.idiomatic: "Zhang Derong is only a dull-witted child—since when is he a guest of state?"

sentences.zh: 」殷曰：「卿勿怪，乃方伯之器也。

translations.literal: Yin said: "Wife, do not marvel; he is the vessel of a regional lord."
translations.idiomatic: You Yin answered, "Do not wonder at this boy—he has the makings of a frontier commander."

sentences.zh: 」殷遂與旣論霸王之略。

translations.literal: Yin thereupon with Ji discussed the strategy of hegemons and kings.
translations.idiomatic: He then sat down with Zhang Ji and discussed the grand strategy of empire.

sentences.zh: 饗訖，以子楚託之；

translations.literal: When the feasting finished, he entrusted his son Chu to him;
translations.idiomatic: When the meal ended, he entrusted his son You Chu to Zhang Ji's care;

sentences.zh: 旣謙不受，殷固託之，旣以殷邦之宿望，難違其旨，乃許之。

translations.literal: Ji modestly refused to accept; Yin firmly entrusted him; because Yin was the commandery's long-standing object of respect, it was hard to violate his purpose, and he thereupon promised.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji demurred until You Yin pressed the charge; unwilling to slight so respected an elder, he finally gave his word.

sentences.zh: 殷先與司隷校尉胡軫有隙，軫誣搆殺殷。

translations.literal: Yin earlier had a rift with the Colonel Director of Retainers Hu Zhen; Zhen slanderously framed and killed Yin.
translations.idiomatic: You Yin had long feuded with metropolitan commandant Hu Zhen, who trumped up charges and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 殷死月餘，軫得疾患，自說但言「伏罪，伏罪，游功曹將鬼來」。

translations.literal: More than a month after Yin died, Zhen contracted illness; he himself spoke only "I confess guilt, I confess guilt—Merit Clerk You is bringing ghosts."
translations.idiomatic: A month later Hu Zhen fell ill, raving nothing but "I confess—Merit Clerk You is coming for me with ghosts."

sentences.zh: 於是遂死。

translations.literal: Thereupon he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died on the spot.

sentences.zh: 于時關中稱曰：「生有知人之明，死有貴神之靈。

translations.literal: At the time Guanzhong proclaimed: "In life he had the clarity to know men; in death he had the numinous power of a noble spirit."
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong folk said of You Yin, "Alive, he knew how to pick men; dead, he still knew how to haunt his killer."

sentences.zh: 」子楚字仲允，為蒲阪令。

translations.literal: The son Chu, courtesy name Zhongyun, was magistrate of Puban.
translations.idiomatic: You Chu, courtesy Zhongyun, later served as magistrate of Puban.

sentences.zh: 太祖定關中時，漢興郡缺，太祖以問旣，旣稱楚才兼文武，遂以為漢興太守。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor pacified Guanzhong, the commandery of Hanxing lacked an incumbent; the Grand Progenitor asked Ji, and Ji praised Chu as combining civil and military talent; thereupon he made him Administrator of Hanxing.
translations.idiomatic: While Cao Cao was pacifying Guanzhong the Hanxing prefecture fell vacant; asked for a nominee, Zhang Ji praised You Chu as a man of both pen and sword, and You Chu received the post.

sentences.zh: 後轉隴西。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was later rotated to Longxi.

sentences.zh: 《魏略》曰：楚為人慷慨，歷位宰守，所在以恩德為治，不好刑殺。

translations.literal: The Wei lue says: Chu as a person was magnanimous; passing through positions as governor, wherever he went he used grace and virtue to govern and did not like punishments and killing.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei lue describes You Chu as open-handed; in every magistracy he ruled by kindness rather than the executioner's block.

sentences.zh: 太和中，諸葛亮出隴右，吏民騷動。

translations.literal: In the Taihe period Zhuge Liang came out on the Longyou flank; clerks and commoners were in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe era Zhuge Liang drove into Longxi and the whole region trembled.

sentences.zh: 天水、南安太守各棄郡東下，楚獨據隴西，召會吏民，謂之曰：「太守無恩德。

translations.literal: The Administrators of Tianshui and Nan'an each abandoned their commanderies and fled east; Chu alone held Longxi, summoned and assembled clerks and commoners, and said to them: "The Administrator lacks grace and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The prefects of Tianshui and Nan'an bolted eastward, but You Chu stayed put in Longxi, called his officials together, and told them, "Your magistrate has done little enough for you.

sentences.zh: 今蜀兵至，諸郡吏民皆已應之，此亦諸卿富貴之秋也。

translations.literal: Now the Shu army has arrived; the clerks and common people of the various commanderies have already responded to them—this too is the autumn of wealth and honor for you gentlemen."
translations.idiomatic: The Shu columns are at the border and every neighboring county has gone over—some might call this your chance for rank and riches."

sentences.zh: 太守本為國家守郡，義在必死，卿諸人便可取太守頭持往。

translations.literal: The Administrator originally for the state guarded the commandery; in righteousness it is certain death—you gentlemen may take the Administrator's head and hold it to go forward."
translations.idiomatic: I was charged to hold this land for Wei, and honor demands I die here—if you prefer Shu, take my head as your passport."

sentences.zh: 」吏民皆涕淚，言「死生當與明府同，無有二心」。

translations.literal: The clerks and common people all wept tears, saying "In death and life we shall be with the enlightened prefect; there is no second heart."
translations.idiomatic: His clerks wept and swore, "We live or die with you, my lord—we will not turn."

sentences.zh: 楚復言：「卿曹若不願，我為卿畫一計。

translations.literal: Chu again spoke: "If you all are not willing, I for you will draw up one plan.
translations.idiomatic: You Chu went on, "If that is not what you want, hear another course.

sentences.zh: 今東二郡已去，必將寇來，但可共堅守。

translations.literal: Now the two eastern commanderies have gone; the enemy is sure to come—you can only hold fast together.
translations.idiomatic: The two eastern commanderies are already gone; the enemy will strike next—our sole hope is a common defense.

sentences.zh: 若國家救到，寇必去，是為一郡守義，人人獲爵寵也。

translations.literal: If the state's rescue arrives, the bandits are sure to depart—this is one commandery guarding righteousness, and every man obtains enfeoffment and favor.
translations.idiomatic: If imperial reinforcements arrive, the Shu army will lift the siege, and every defender will earn titles and reward.

sentences.zh: 若官救不到，蜀攻日急，爾乃取太守以降，未為晚也。

translations.literal: If official rescue does not arrive and Shu attacks daily more urgently, only then take the Administrator to surrender—not late."
