translations.idiomatic: If no help comes and the Shu pressure grows unbearable, then deliver me up—not before."

sentences.zh: 」吏民遂城守。

translations.literal: The clerks and common people thereupon walled and defended.
translations.idiomatic: The people accepted the plan and manned the walls.

sentences.zh: 而南安果將蜀兵，就攻隴西。

translations.literal: And Nan'an indeed led Shu troops and thereupon attacked Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Nan'an's defectors soon led Shu troops against Longxi.

sentences.zh: 楚聞賊到，乃遣長史馬顒出門設陣，而自於城上曉謂蜀帥，言：「卿能斷隴，使東兵不上，一月之中，則隴西吏人不攻自服；

translations.literal: When Chu heard the bandits had arrived, he thereupon sent Chief Clerk Ma Yan out the gate to set battle lines, while he himself on the city wall at dawn addressed the Shu commander, saying: "If you can cut the Long road and make eastern troops unable to come up, within one month then the clerks and people of Longxi will submit without attack;
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the enemy approach, You Chu sent chief clerk Ma Yan to draw up outside the walls while he himself hailed the Shu commander from the parapet: "Seal the Long defile so relief cannot march west, and within a month Longxi will yield without a blow;

sentences.zh: 卿若不能，虛自疲弊耳。

translations.literal: If you cannot, vainly you will exhaust yourselves."
translations.idiomatic: fail in that, and you will only wear yourselves out for nothing."

sentences.zh: 」使顒鳴鼓擊之，蜀人乃去。

translations.literal: He ordered Yan to beat drums and strike them; the Shu people thereupon departed.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Ma Yan to beat the war drums; the Shu force withdrew.

sentences.zh: 後十餘日，諸軍上隴，諸葛亮破走。

translations.literal: After more than ten days the various armies ascended the Long; Zhuge Liang was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days later Wei columns cleared the Long defile and Zhuge Liang broke off the siege.

sentences.zh: 南安、天水皆坐應亮破滅，兩郡守各獲重刑，而楚以功封列侯，長史掾屬皆賜拜。

translations.literal: Nan'an and Tianshui both because of responding to Liang were destroyed and broken; the two commandery guardians each received heavy punishment, while Chu by merit was enfeoffed a full marquis, and chief clerks and staff all received grants of appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Tianshui and Nan'an fell for colluding with Shu and their prefects were harshly punished, whereas You Chu won a full marquisate and his staff received honors.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其治，詔特聽朝，引上殿。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his governance, ordered him specially permitted audience at court, and led him up the hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended his rule, summoned him to court, and escorted him personally to the dais.

sentences.zh: 楚為人短小而大聲，自為吏，初不朝覲，被詔登階，不知儀式。

translations.literal: Chu as a person was short in stature but had a great voice; from the time he became a clerk he had never once attended court audience; receiving the edict to ascend the steps, he did not know the ritual forms.
translations.idiomatic: You Chu was a short man with a booming voice; having never attended court, he botched palace etiquette when first summoned.

sentences.zh: 帝令侍中贊引，呼「隴西太守前」，楚當言「唯」，而大應稱「諾」。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the palace attendant to conduct him in, calling "Administrator of Longxi step forward"; Chu ought to have said "Yes" but loudly answered "Understood."
translations.idiomatic: The usher intoned, "Longxi Prefect, advance!"—to which a courtier should murmur "Yes"; You Chu bellowed "Aye!"

sentences.zh: 帝顧之而笑，遂勞勉之。

translations.literal: The emperor looked back at him and laughed, thereupon consoled and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor glanced back, laughed, and kindly put him at ease.

sentences.zh: 罷會，自表乞留宿衞，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: When the meeting dismissed, he personally memorialized begging to remain as palace guard and was appointed Commandant of the Household for All Purposes.
translations.idiomatic: After court he begged leave to remain as an imperial guardsman and was named chief commandant of the household for all purposes.

sentences.zh: 楚不學問，而性好遊遨音樂。

translations.literal: Chu did not pursue learning, yet by nature loved roaming, music.
translations.idiomatic: You Chu cared little for books but doted on travel and music.

sentences.zh: 乃畜歌者，琵琶、箏、簫，每行來將以自隨。

translations.literal: He therefore kept singers, pipa, zheng, and xiao, every time traveling taking them to follow himself.
translations.idiomatic: He kept a troupe of singers and cartloads of pipa, zithers, and flutes wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 所在樗蒲、投壺，歡欣自娛。

translations.literal: Where he went was chupu and pitch-pot, joyous self-amusement.
translations.idiomatic: In every posting he passed the time at dice games and pitch-pot, amusing himself without cease.

sentences.zh: 數歲，復出為北地太守，年七十餘卒。〉

translations.literal: After several years he again went out as Administrator of Beidi, and died at age seventy-some.〉
translations.idiomatic: Years later he returned to the field as prefect of Beidi and died in his seventies.〉

sentences.zh: 是時，武威顏雋、張掖和鸞、酒泉黃華、西平麴演等並舉郡反，自號將軍，更相攻擊。

translations.literal: At this time Yan Jun of Wuwei, He Luan of Zhangye, Huang Hua of Jiuquan, Qu Yan of Xiping, and others together raised their commanderies in rebellion, styled themselves generals, and mutually attacked.
translations.idiomatic: About then Yan Jun in Wuwei, He Luan in Zhangye, Huang Hua in Jiuquan, Qu Yan in Xiping, and others rebelled under their own battle flags and turned on one another.

sentences.zh: 雋遣使送母及子詣太祖為質，求助。

translations.literal: Jun sent envoys to deliver his mother and son to the Grand Progenitor as hostages, seeking aid.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Jun sent his mother and son to Cao Cao as hostages and begged for rescue.

sentences.zh: 太祖問旣，旣曰：「雋等外假國威，內生傲悖，計定勢足，後即反耳。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor asked Ji; Ji said: "Jun and others outwardly borrow state might, inwardly breed arrogance and perversity; when their plans are settled and power sufficient, afterward they will rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao asked Zhang Ji, who answered, "Those men borrow your prestige while nursing their own pride; once secure they will betray you just the same.

sentences.zh: 今方事定蜀，且宜兩存而鬬之，猶卞莊子之刺虎，坐收其斃也。

translations.literal: Now the square affair is settling Shu; for the moment it is fitting to let both survive and make them fight—it is still Bian Zhuangzi's stabbing tigers, sitting and collecting their exhaustion."
translations.idiomatic: You are still busy with Shu; better let these wolves savage each other like Bian Zhuangzi's two tigers—then reap the exhausted survivor."

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「善。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao said, "Excellent."

sentences.zh: 」歲餘，鸞遂殺雋，武威王祕又殺鸞。

translations.literal: After more than a year Luan thereupon killed Jun, and Wang Mi of Wuwei again killed Luan.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year He Luan murdered Yan Jun, then Wang Mi of Wuwei murdered He Luan.

sentences.zh: 是時不置涼州，自三輔拒西域，皆屬雍州。

translations.literal: At this time Liangzhou was not established; from the Three Supports resisting the Western Regions, all belonged to Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzhou had been abolished, and everything from the capital districts westward fell under Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 文帝即王位，初置涼州，以安定太守鄒岐為刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen assumed the king's throne, he first established Liangzhou, appointing the Administrator of Anding Zou Qi as Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Pi took the kingship he revived Liangzhou and named Zou Qi of Anding as its inspector.

sentences.zh: 張掖張進執郡守舉兵拒岐，黃華、麴演各逐故太守，舉兵以應之。

translations.literal: Zhang Jin of Zhangye seized the commandery guardian and raised troops to resist Qi; Huang Hua and Qu Yan each expelled their former administrators and raised troops to respond to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jin of Zhangye imprisoned the sitting prefect and defied Zou Qi; Huang Hua and Qu Yan drove out their magistrates and joined the revolt.

sentences.zh: 旣進兵為護羌校尉蘇則聲勢，故則得以有功。

translations.literal: Ji advanced troops to lend Colonel Who Protects the Qiang Su Ze momentum, therefore Ze was able to have merit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji marched in support of Su Ze, the Qiang protector, which let Su Ze win his victory.

sentences.zh: 旣進爵都鄉侯。

translations.literal: Ji advanced in noble rank to Village Marquis of the Capital District.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji was promoted to metropolitan village marquis.

sentences.zh: 涼州盧水胡伊健妓妾、治元多等反，河西大擾。

translations.literal: The Lu-shui Hu of Liangzhou, Yi Jianjiqie, Zhi Yuanduo, and others rebelled, and the west of the river was greatly disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: The Lu-shui Hu chieftains Yi Jianjiqie and Zhi Yuanduo rose in Liangzhou and threw the Hexi corridor into chaos.

sentences.zh: 帝憂之，曰：「非旣莫能安涼州。

translations.literal: The emperor worried over it, saying: "If not Ji none can pacify Liangzhou."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fretted aloud, "Only Zhang Ji can quiet Liangzhou."

sentences.zh: 」乃召鄒岐，以旣代之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he summoned Zou Qi and replaced him with Ji.
translations.idiomatic: He recalled Zou Qi and sent Zhang Ji west in his stead.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「昔賈復請擊郾賊，光武笑曰：『執金吾擊郾，吾復何憂？

translations.literal: The edict said: "Formerly Jia Fu requested to strike the Yan bandits; Guangwu laughed and said, The Bearer of the Golden Mace strikes Yan—what more have I to worry about from Jia Fu?"
translations.idiomatic: His rescript read: "When Jia Fu begged to crush the Yan rebels, Guangwu laughed and said that with his golden-mace guard leading the attack he had nothing left to fear."

sentences.zh: 』卿謀略過人，今則其時。

translations.literal: Your planning and strategy surpass others; now is its time.
translations.idiomatic: "Your stratagems outclass any rival—this is the moment to use them."

sentences.zh: 以便宜從事，勿復先請。

translations.literal: Act at convenience in handling affairs; do not again first request."
translations.idiomatic: "Act on your own authority; do not wait for prior approval."

sentences.zh: 」遣護軍夏侯儒、將軍費曜等繼其後。

translations.literal: He dispatched Protector of the Army Xiahou Ru, General Fei Yao, and others to follow his rear.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Xiahou Ru and Fei Yao to follow with supporting columns.

sentences.zh: 旣至金城，欲渡河，諸將守以為「兵少道險，未可深入」。

translations.literal: When Ji reached Jincheng, wishing to cross the river, the various generals guarding thought "troops are few and the road perilous; one cannot deeply penetrate."
translations.idiomatic: At Jincheng Zhang Ji meant to ford the Yellow River; his officers protested that the column was too small and the terrain too treacherous.

sentences.zh: 旣曰：「道雖險，非井陘之隘，夷狄烏合，無左車之計，今武威危急，赴之宜速。

translations.literal: Ji said: "Though the road is perilous, it is not the narrowness of Jingxing; the Yi and Di are a crow flock without Zuo Che's stratagem; now Wuwei is critically urgent—hastening to aid it is fitting."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji answered, "The defile is bad, but nothing like Jingxing; these barbarians are a rabble without Li Zuoche's wit; Wuwei is burning—speed is everything."

sentences.zh: 」遂渡河。

translations.literal: Thereupon he crossed the river.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the river at once.

sentences.zh: 賊七千餘騎逆拒軍於鸇陰口，旣揚聲軍從鸇陰，乃潛由且次出至武威。

translations.literal: Bandits more than seven thousand horse met and resisted the army at Zanyin Pass; Ji raised a cry that the army would follow Zanyin, then secretly by Qieci went out and reached Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: Seven thousand enemy horse blocked Zanyin Pass; Zhang Ji feinted toward Zanyin, then slipped along a side valley to emerge at Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 胡以為神，引還顯美。

translations.literal: The Hu thought it supernatural and led away returning to Xianmei.
translations.idiomatic: The Hu took him for a god, broke, and fled toward Xianmei.

sentences.zh: 旣已據武威，曜乃至，儒等猶未達。

translations.literal: Ji having already occupied Wuwei, Yao then arrived, and Ru and others still had not reached.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji was already in Wuwei when Fei Yao arrived; Xiahou Ru still lagged behind.

sentences.zh: 旣勞賜將士，欲進軍擊胡。

translations.literal: Ji rewarded and feasted officers and soldiers, wished to advance the army to strike the Hu.
translations.idiomatic: He feasted the troops and prepared to strike the Hu.

sentences.zh: 諸將皆曰：「士卒疲倦，虜衆氣銳，難與爭鋒。

translations.literal: The various generals all said: "The soldiers are weary; the enemy masses' qi is sharp; it is hard to contend for the point."
translations.idiomatic: His generals objected: "The men are spent and the nomads are fresh—this is no time to joust."

sentences.zh: 」旣曰：「今軍無見糧，當因敵為資。

translations.literal: Ji said: "Now the army has no visible grain; we ought to take the enemy as supply."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji said, "We carry no grain—our only commissary is the enemy camp."

sentences.zh: 若虜見兵合，退依深山，追之則道險窮餓，兵還則出候寇鈔。

translations.literal: If the barbarians see the troops unite, withdraw and rely on deep mountains, pursuing them then the road is perilous and they end in starvation; if the troops return then they go out waiting to raid.
translations.idiomatic: Let them rally in the hills and we starve chasing them; let us turn back and they raid our rear.

sentences.zh: 如此，兵不得解，所謂『一日縱敵，患在數世』也。

translations.literal: Like this the troops cannot be released—what is called "one day letting the enemy go, the calamity is in several generations."
translations.idiomatic: That is the mischief the histories call "spare the foe for one day, breed trouble for generations."

sentences.zh: 」遂前軍顯美。

translations.literal: Thereupon he advanced the army to Xianmei.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed straight to Xianmei.

sentences.zh: 胡騎數千，因大風欲放火燒營，將士皆恐。

translations.literal: Hu cavalry in the thousands, relying on a great wind, wished to set fire and burn the camp; officers and soldiers all feared.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands of Hu horse tried to burn the camp when a gale sprang up, and panic spread through the ranks.

sentences.zh: 旣夜藏精卒三千人為伏，使參軍成公英督千餘騎挑戰，勑使陽退。

translations.literal: Ji by night hid crack troops three thousand men as an ambush, had Army Consultant Cheng Gongying supervise more than a thousand horse to challenge battle, ordered them feignedly to retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji hid three thousand picked men by night, sent staff officer Cheng Gongying forward with a thousand horse in a sham retreat.

sentences.zh: 胡果爭奔之，因發伏截其後，首尾進擊，大破之，斬首獲生以萬數。

translations.literal: The Hu indeed scrambled to pursue them; thereupon he released the ambush to cut their rear, head and tail advancing to strike, greatly defeated them, beheading and capturing alive by the ten thousand count.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hu rushed the bait, the ambush closed on their rear; front and rear hammered them, killing and capturing by the myriad.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：成公英，金城人也。

translations.literal: The Wei lue says: Cheng Gongying was a man of Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei lue identifies Cheng Gongying as a native of Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 中平末，隨韓約為腹心。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhongping era he followed Han Yue as intimate confidant.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Zhongping reign he became a trusted follower of Han Yue (Han Sui).

sentences.zh: 建安中，約從華陰破走，還湟中，部黨散去，唯英獨從。

translations.literal: In the Jian'an era Yue followed defeat and flight from Huayin, returned to the Huangzhong region, tribal followers scattered and left, only Ying alone followed.
translations.idiomatic: After Han Sui's rout at Huayin in the Jian'an years his host melted away—only Cheng Gongying stayed at his side.

sentences.zh: 《典略》曰：韓遂在湟中，其壻閻行欲殺遂以降，夜攻遂，不下。

translations.literal: The Dian lue says: Han Sui was in the Huangzhong region; his son-in-law Yan Xing wished to kill Sui to surrender, attacked Sui by night, did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: The Dian lue adds that while Han Sui sheltered in the Huang riverlands his son-in-law Yan Xing tried to murder him and defect, but the night attack failed.

sentences.zh: 遂歎息曰：「丈夫困厄，禍起婚姻乎！

translations.literal: Sui sighed and said: "A great man in distress—does calamity arise from marriage!"
translations.idiomatic: Han Sui sighed, "So a hero's ruin begins in his own family!"

sentences.zh: 」謂英曰：「今親戚離叛，人衆轉少，當從羌中西南詣蜀耳。

translations.literal: He said to Ying: "Now kin have rebelled and left, the multitude has turned fewer; we ought from among the Qiang go southwest to Shu."
translations.idiomatic: He told Cheng Gongying, "My kin have deserted me and my following has shrunk—we should cut southwest through the Qiang country into Shu."

sentences.zh: 」英曰：「興軍數十年，今雖罷敗，何有棄其門而依於人乎！

translations.literal: Ying said: "Raising armies several tens of years, now though defeated and broken, how is there abandoning one's gate and relying on others!"
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Gongying retorted, "We have borne arms for decades; defeat is no reason to flee our home ground and cling to another lord."

sentences.zh: 」遂曰：「吾年老矣，子欲何施？

translations.literal: Sui said: "I am old; what do you intend to do?"
translations.idiomatic: Han Sui said, "I am an old man—what plan do you offer?"

sentences.zh: 」英曰：「曹公不能遠來，獨夏侯爾。

translations.literal: Ying said: "Lord Cao cannot come from afar; it is only Xiahou."
translations.idiomatic: "Cao Cao will not march this far himself—only Xiahou Yuan."

sentences.zh: 夏侯之衆，不足以追我，又不能乆留；

translations.literal: Xiahou's masses are not enough to pursue us, nor able to stay long;
translations.idiomatic: His column is too small to run us down and too ill supplied to loiter.

sentences.zh: 且息肩於羌中，以須其去。

translations.literal: for the moment rest shoulders among the Qiang and await his departure.
translations.idiomatic: Let us rest among the Qiang until he withdraws."

sentences.zh: 招呼故人，綏會羌、胡，猶可以有為也。

translations.literal: Summon old friends, pacify and assemble Qiang and Hu, and still there can be accomplishment."
translations.idiomatic: "Recall our old allies, rally the Qiang and Hu, and we may yet recover."

sentences.zh: 」遂從其計，時隨從者男女尚數千人。

translations.literal: Sui followed his plan; at the time followers male and female still numbered several thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: Han Sui agreed; he still had a few thousand followers, women and children among them.

sentences.zh: 遂宿有恩於羌，羌衞護之。

translations.literal: Sui long had grace among the Qiang; the Qiang guarded and protected him.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang remembered his past kindness and shielded him.

sentences.zh: 及夏侯淵還，使閻行留後。

translations.literal: When Xiahou Yuan returned, he had Yan Xing remain behind.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiahou Yuan pulled back he left Yan Xing to hold the rear.

sentences.zh: 乃合羌、胡數萬將攻行，行欲走，會遂死，英降太祖。

translations.literal: Thereupon he united Qiang and Hu numbering several tens of thousands intending to attack Xing; Xing wished to flee; it happened Sui died, and Ying surrendered to the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: Han Sui then raised tens of thousands of Qiang and Hu against Yan Xing, who prepared to bolt; Han Sui died in the midst of it, and Cheng Gongying came over to Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 太祖見英甚喜，以為軍師，封列侯。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor seeing Ying was very pleased, made him army adviser, enfeoffed a full marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao received Cheng Gongying with delight, named him army adviser, and enfeoffed him a full marquis.

sentences.zh: 從行出獵，有三鹿走過前，公命英射之，三發三中，皆應弦而倒。

translations.literal: Following on a hunt going out, three deer ran past in front; the lord ordered Ying to shoot them; three releases three hits, all with the string's sound fell.
translations.idiomatic: On a hunt three deer bounded past; Cao Cao told him to shoot—three arrows, three deer, each dropping at the twang.

sentences.zh: 公抵掌謂之曰：「但韓文約可為盡節，而孤獨不可乎？

translations.literal: The lord clapped palms and said to him: "Only Han Wenyue could have one exhaust loyalty, yet I alone cannot?"
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao clapped and said, "You gave Han Sui your utmost—will you give me nothing?"

sentences.zh: 」英乃下馬而跪曰：「不欺明公。

translations.literal: Ying thereupon dismounted horse and knelt saying: "I do not deceive the enlightened lord.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Gongying slipped from the saddle and knelt. "I would not lie to you, my lord.

sentences.zh: 假使英本主人在，實不來此也。

translations.literal: Supposing my original master were present, in truth I would not have come here."
translations.idiomatic: Had my old master still lived, I would never have ridden to your camp."

sentences.zh: 」遂流涕哽咽。

translations.literal: Thereupon he wept tears and choked.
translations.idiomatic: He broke down sobbing.

sentences.zh: 公嘉其敦舊，遂親敬之。

translations.literal: The lord praised his honest attachment to the old, thereupon personally respected him.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao honored his stubborn loyalty to a lost cause and treated him thereafter with personal respect.

sentences.zh: 延康、黃初之際，河西有逆謀。

translations.literal: Between the Yankang and Huangchu periods there was treasonous plotting in Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: Around the change from Yankang to Huangchu, the Hexi corridor seethed with plots of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 詔遣英佐涼州平隴右，病卒。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched Ying to assist Liangzhou in pacifying Longyou; he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Cheng Gongying west to help pacify Longyou; he died on duty.

sentences.zh: 《魏略》曰：閻行，金城人也，後名艷，字彥明。

translations.literal: The Wei lue says: Yan Xing was a man of Jincheng; later his name was changed to Yan, courtesy name Yanming.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei lue identifies Yan Xing of Jincheng, who later took the single-character surname Yan and the courtesy name Yanming.

sentences.zh: 少有健名，始為小將，隨韓約。

translations.literal: In youth he had a reputation for vigor; he first was a minor general following Han Yue.
translations.idiomatic: He was famed as a fighter in his youth and began as a junior officer under Han Sui.

sentences.zh: 建安初，約與馬騰相攻擊。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jian'an, Yue and Ma Teng mutually attacked.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jian'an era Han Sui and Ma Teng fought each other repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 騰子超亦號為健。

translations.literal: Teng's son Chao also was styled vigorous.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Teng's son Ma Chao enjoyed the same reputation for toughness.

sentences.zh: 行嘗刺超，矛折，因以折矛撾超項，幾殺之。

translations.literal: Xing once stabbed Chao; the spear broke, and therefore with the broken spear he struck Chao's neck, nearly killing him.
translations.idiomatic: In one clash Yan Xing's spear snapped against Ma Chao; he clubbed Ma Chao across the neck with the splintered shaft and nearly killed him.

sentences.zh: 至十四年，為約所使詣太祖，太祖厚遇之，表拜犍為太守。

translations.literal: By the fourteenth year he was dispatched by Yue to visit the Grand Progenitor; the Grand Progenitor treated him generously and memorialized appointing him Administrator of Qianwei.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Jian'an Han Sui sent him to Cao Cao, who received him lavishly and had him named prefect of Qianwei.

sentences.zh: 行因請令其父入宿衞，西還見約，宣太祖教云：「謝文約：卿始起兵時，自有所逼，我所具明也。

translations.literal: Xing thereupon requested to have his father enter palace guard duty, returned west to see Yue, and proclaimed the Grand Progenitor's instruction saying: "I thank Wenyue: when you first raised troops, you yourself had something compelling you—I have made that fully clear.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Xing asked to leave his father as a hostage in the capital, rode back to Han Sui, and delivered Cao Cao's message: "Tell Wenyue I know he took up arms under duress at first—that has never been in doubt.

sentences.zh: 當早來，共匡輔國朝。

translations.literal: You ought early to come and together assist and support the dynastic court."
translations.idiomatic: Tell him to come in soon and help set the house of Wei to rights."

sentences.zh: 」行因謂約曰：「行亦為將軍，興軍以來三十餘年，民兵疲瘁，所處又狹，宜早自附。

translations.literal: Xing thereupon said to Yue: "Xing also is for the general; since raising armies more than thirty years, militia and people are weary and wasted, and the place where we dwell is again narrow—it is fitting early to attach yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Yan Xing then urged Han Sui, "I have ridden with you for thirty years; our men are exhausted and our lands cramped—it is time to submit while we still can."

sentences.zh: 是以前在鄴，自啟當令老父詣京師，誠謂將軍亦宜遣一子，以示丹赤。

translations.literal: This is why formerly at Ye I personally explained that I would have my aged father go to the capital; truly I thought the general also ought to dispatch one son, thereby showing crimson loyalty."
translations.idiomatic: That is why I volunteered my old father as a hostage at Ye; I hoped you would send a son as well, to show the court your good faith."

sentences.zh: 」約曰：「且可復觀望數歲中！

translations.literal: Yue said: "For the moment one can again watch and wait several years within!"
translations.idiomatic: Han Sui answered, "Let us watch how the wind blows a few years longer."

sentences.zh: 」後遂遣其子，與行父母俱東。

translations.literal: Afterward he thereupon dispatched his son, together with Xing's parents both east.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he did send a son east, along with Yan Xing's parents.

sentences.zh: 會約西討張猛，留行守舊營，而馬超等結反謀，舉約為都督。

translations.literal: It happened Yue campaigned west against Zhang Meng, left Xing to guard the old camp, while Ma Chao and others formed a treasonous plot, raising Yue as commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Sui marched west against Zhang Meng he left Yan Xing in charge of the base; Ma Chao and his allies then plotted revolt and named Han Sui their commander.

sentences.zh: 及約還，超謂約曰：「前鍾司隷任超使取將軍，關東人不可復信也。

translations.literal: When Yue returned, Chao said to Yue: "Formerly Colonel Zhong appointed Chao to seize the general; men east of the pass cannot again be trusted.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Sui came back, Ma Chao told him, "Zhong Yao once ordered me to arrest you—easterners cannot be trusted."

sentences.zh: 今超棄父，以將軍為父，將軍亦當棄子，以超為子。

translations.literal: Now Chao has cast aside his father and takes the general as father; the general also ought to cast aside his son and take Chao as son."
translations.idiomatic: I have abandoned my father to follow you; you must abandon your son and treat me as your heir."

sentences.zh: 」行諫約，不欲令與超合。

translations.literal: Xing remonstrated with Yue, not wishing to let him join with Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Xing pleaded with Han Sui not to bind himself to Ma Chao.

sentences.zh: 約謂行曰：「今諸將不謀而同，似有天數。

translations.literal: Yue said to Xing: "Now the various generals plot alike without consulting—it seems there is a heavenly reckoning."
translations.idiomatic: Han Sui replied, "Every captain has reached the same decision without a meeting—perhaps fate wills it."

sentences.zh: 」乃東詣華陰。

translations.literal: Thereupon he went east to Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore rode east to Huayin with the rebels.

sentences.zh: 及太祖與約交馬語，行在其後，太祖望謂行曰：「當念作孝子。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor and Yue crossed horses and spoke, Xing was behind him; the Grand Progenitor looked afar and said to Xing: "You ought to remember to be a filial son."
translations.idiomatic: At the parley between Cao Cao and Han Sui, Yan Xing rode in Han Sui's train; Cao Cao called out, "Remember your duty as a son."

sentences.zh: 」及超等破走，行隨約還金城。

translations.literal: When Chao and others were defeated and fled, Xing followed Yue back to Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: After Ma Chao's rout Yan Xing retreated with Han Sui to Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞行前意，故但誅約子孫在京師者。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor heard Xing's earlier intention, therefore only executed Yue's sons and grandsons who were in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of Yan Xing's earlier loyalty, Cao Cao executed only those of Han Sui's kin who were actually in the capital.

sentences.zh: 乃手書與行曰：「觀文約所為，使人笑來。

translations.literal: Thereupon he personally wrote to Xing saying: "Observing Wenyue's conduct makes one burst out laughing.
translations.idiomatic: He then wrote privately to Yan Xing: "Han Wenyue's antics would make any man laugh aloud.

sentences.zh: 吾前後與之書，無所不說，如此何可復忍！

translations.literal: My letters to him before and after left nothing unsaid—how can one again endure this!"
translations.idiomatic: I have told him everything in letter after letter—how much more of this am I expected to swallow?"

sentences.zh: 卿父諫議，自平安也。

translations.literal: Your father the remonstrator is personally safe.
translations.idiomatic: Your father, the adviser, is safe for the moment.

sentences.zh: 雖然，牢獄之中，非養親之處，且又官家亦不能乆為人養老也。

translations.literal: Although it is so, inside prison is not a place to nourish kin, and moreover the official family also cannot long for others nurture the aged."
translations.idiomatic: Still, a jail is no home for an old man, and the state cannot feed him forever."

sentences.zh: 」約聞行父獨在，欲使並遇害，以一其心，乃彊以少女妻行，行不獲已。

translations.literal: Yue heard Xing's father alone survived, wished to make them together meet harm so as to unify his heart, therefore forced a young daughter on Xing as wife; Xing had no choice but accept.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that only Yan Xing's father still lived, Han Sui tried to embroil both in ruin to bind Yan Xing to him—he forced his own young daughter on Yan Xing as a wife, and Yan Xing could not refuse.

sentences.zh: 太祖果疑行。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor indeed suspected Xing.
translations.idiomatic: The marriage made Cao Cao doubt Yan Xing's loyalty.

sentences.zh: 會約使行別領西平郡。

translations.literal: It happened Yue ordered Xing separately to lead Xiping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Han Sui then detached Yan Xing to command Xiping.

sentences.zh: 遂勒其部曲，與約相攻擊。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led his following and with Yue mutually attacked.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Xing turned his retainers against his old patron and attacked Han Sui.

sentences.zh: 行不勝，乃將家人東詣太祖。

translations.literal: Xing did not prevail, thereupon led family members east to visit the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: Beaten, he shepherded his household east to surrender to Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 太祖表拜列侯。〉

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor memorialized appointing him a full marquis.〉
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao had him enfeoffed a full marquis.〉

sentences.zh: 帝甚恱，詔曰：「卿踰河歷險，以勞擊逸，以寡勝衆，功過南仲，勤踰吉甫。

translations.literal: The emperor was very pleased; the edict said: "You crossed the river and passed through peril, used labor to strike ease, used few to overcome many; merit surpasses Nan Zhong, diligence surpasses Ji Fu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and wrote: "You braved the river and its dangers, struck a rested foe with weary troops, and overcame great numbers with a handful—your service outshines Nan Zhong, your zeal outdoes Yin Jifu.

sentences.zh: 此勳非但破胡，乃永寧河右，使吾長無西顧之念矣。

translations.literal: This merit is not only smashing the Hu—it is eternally pacifying the west of the river, causing me long to have no thought of looking west."
translations.idiomatic: You have done more than crush the barbarians: you have given the Hexi corridor lasting peace so that I need never again fear the western horizon."

sentences.zh: 」徙封西鄉侯，增邑二百，並前四百戶。

translations.literal: He was transferred enfeoffment to Marquis of Xixiang, increased fief by two hundred households, together with the previous four hundred households."
translations.idiomatic: His fief was moved to Xixiang village, with two hundred extra households added to the four hundred he already held."

sentences.zh: 酒泉蘇衡反，與羌豪鄰戴及丁令胡萬餘騎攻邊縣。

translations.literal: Su Heng of Jiuquan rebelled, together with Qiang magnate Lin Dai and Dingling Hu more than ten thousand horse attacked border counties.
translations.idiomatic: Su Heng of Jiuquan rose with the Qiang chief Lin Dai and over ten thousand Dingling Hu horsemen to raid the frontier counties.

sentences.zh: 旣與夏侯儒擊破之，衡及鄰戴等皆降。

translations.literal: Ji together with Xiahou Ru defeated them; Heng and Lin Dai and others all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji and Xiahou Ru broke their force; Su Heng, Lin Dai, and their allies capitulated.

sentences.zh: 遂上疏請與儒治左城，築鄣塞，置烽候、邸閣以備胡。

translations.literal: Thereupon he submitted a memorial requesting together with Ru to administer Zuocheng, build barrier walls, establish beacon watchtowers and relay lodges to prepare against the Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji then memorialized for leave to work with Xiahou Ru on fortifying Zuocheng—palisades, beacon chains, and courier stations against further nomad raids.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：儒字雋林，夏侯尚從弟。

translations.literal: The Wei lue says: Ru's courtesy name was Juanlin, a cousin of Xiahou Shang.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei lue gives Xiahou Ru's style as Juanlin, a cousin of Xiahou Shang.

sentences.zh: 初為鄢陵侯彰驍騎司馬，宣王為征南將軍，都督荊、豫州。

translations.literal: At first he was swift-cavalry major to Marquis Yanling Cao Zhang; the King of Xuan was General Who Conquers the South, commander-in-chief of Jing and Yu provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He began as chief of swift cavalry under Cao Zhang, marquis of Yanling, while Sima Yi held the southern command over Jing and Yu.

sentences.zh: 正始二年，朱然圍樊城，城中守將乙脩等求救甚急。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengshi Zhu Ran besieged Fancheng; defenders such as Yi Xiu inside the city sought rescue with extreme urgency.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengshi 2 Zhu Ran invested Fancheng, and the garrison commander Yi Xiu pleaded desperately for relief.

sentences.zh: 儒進屯鄧塞，以兵少不敢進，但作鼓吹，設導從，去然六七里，翱翔而還，使脩等遙見之，數數如是。

translations.literal: Ru advanced and encamped at Dengsai; because troops were few he did not dare advance, but only set up drums and wind music, arranged guides and followers, went six or seven li from Zhu Ran, wheeled and returned, had Xiu and others see him from afar, repeatedly thus.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Ru halted at Dengsai with too few men to attack, yet staged a parade—music, banners, a slow ride within sight of the walls, then a withdrawal—repeating the charade for weeks to buoy the defenders' spirits.

sentences.zh: 月餘，及太傅到，乃俱進，然等走。

translations.literal: After more than a month when the Grand Tutor arrived, then together they advanced, and Zhu Ran and others fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Yi arrived a month later, the combined columns advanced and Zhu Ran lifted the siege.

sentences.zh: 時謂儒為怯，或以為曉以少疑衆，得聲救之宜。

translations.literal: At the time they called Ru cowardly, or some thought he understood using few to make the multitude doubtful, obtaining the propriety of a feigned rescue shout.
translations.idiomatic: Some mocked him as timid; others argued he had bluffed a larger host with a handful, the classic stratagem of sounding a false relief.

sentences.zh: 儒猶以此召還，為太僕。〉

translations.literal: Ru still because of this was summoned back and became Minister Coachman.〉
translations.idiomatic: Even so he was recalled and given the sinceure of minister coachman.〉

sentences.zh: 西羌恐，率衆二萬餘落降。

translations.literal: The Western Qiang feared and led their masses, more than twenty thousand households, to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Western Qiang bands, over twenty thousand tents, submitted in fear.

sentences.zh: 其後西平麴光等殺其郡守，諸將欲擊之，旣曰：「唯光等造反，郡人未必悉同。

translations.literal: Afterward Qu Guang and others of Xiping killed their commandery guardian; the various generals wished to strike them; Ji said: "Only Guang and others rebel; the people of the commandery are not necessarily all the same.
translations.idiomatic: Later Qu Guang of Xiping murdered his prefect; generals clamored to attack, but Zhang Ji said, "Only Qu Guang's clique is guilty—the county need not share their guilt.

sentences.zh: 若便以軍臨之，吏民羌胡必謂國家不別是非，更使皆相持著，此為虎傅翼也。

translations.literal: If immediately you use the army to press them, clerks, commoners, Qiang, and Hu will surely say the state does not distinguish right and wrong, further causing all mutually to hold fast—this is for the tiger to add wings."
translations.idiomatic: Send troops now and every clerk, farmer, Qiang, and Hu will think the court blind to justice—they will lock arms with the rebels and hand the tiger its wings."

sentences.zh: 光等欲以羌胡為援，今先使羌胡鈔擊，重其賞募，所虜獲者皆以畀之。

translations.literal: Guang and others wish to use Qiang and Hu as support; now first cause Qiang and Hu to raid and strike them, double their rewards for enlistment, and what is captured and seized all give to them.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Guang counts on Qiang and Hu allies—turn those allies against him first: double the bounty on his head and let the tribes keep every captive and herd they take."

sentences.zh: 外沮其勢，內離其交，必不戰而定。

translations.literal: Outwardly block their momentum, inwardly split their alliance—without battle it will be settled."
translations.idiomatic: Throttle him from without, split him from within, and he will fall without a pitched battle."

sentences.zh: 」乃檄告諭諸羌，為光等所詿誤者原之；

translations.literal: Thereupon he issued a proclamation instructing the various Qiang: those misled by Guang and others he pardoned;
translations.idiomatic: He issued a proclamation to the Qiang bands, pardoning any who had been duped by Qu Guang;

sentences.zh: 能斬賊帥送首者當加封賞。

translations.literal: whoever could behead the bandit chieftains and deliver heads would receive added enfeoffment and reward.
translations.idiomatic: and promising noble rank to whoever brought him the rebels' heads.

sentences.zh: 於是光部黨斬送光首，其餘咸安堵如故。

translations.literal: Thereupon Guang's partisans beheaded and sent Guang's head; the rest all were peaceful and settled as before.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Guang's own followers cut off his head; everyone else went quietly back to their fields.

sentences.zh: 子 緝

translations.literal: Son: Ji (same graph as the father's given name in the text).
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhang Ji.

sentences.zh: 緝以中書郎稍遷東莞太守。

translations.literal: Ji from Palace Secretariat Gentleman gradually was promoted Administrator of Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhang Ji rose from gentleman of the palace secretariat to prefect of Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 嘉平中，女為皇后，徵拜光祿大夫，位特進，封妻向為安城鄉君。

translations.literal: In the Jiaping period his daughter became empress; he was summoned and appointed Grand Master of Splendid Carriage, rank specially advanced, enfeoffed his wife Xiang as Lady of Ancheng Village.
translations.idiomatic: During Jiaping his daughter entered the palace as empress; he was recalled as grand master of splendid carriage with specially advanced rank, and his wife Xiang was titled lady of Ancheng village.

sentences.zh: 緝與中書令李豐同謀，誅。

translations.literal: Ji together with Palace Secretariat Director Li Feng plotted together and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: He joined director Li Feng's plot and died for it.

sentences.zh: 語在《夏侯玄傳》。

translations.literal: The account is in the "Biography of Xiahou Xuan."
translations.idiomatic: The story is told in the biography of Xiahou Xuan.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：緝字敬仲，太和中為溫令，名有治能。

translations.literal: The Wei lue says: Ji's courtesy name was Jingzhong; in the Taihe period he was magistrate of Wen, famous for governing ability.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei lue names him Zhang Ji, style Jingzhong, who as magistrate of Wen during Taihe earned a reputation for competence.

sentences.zh: 會諸葛亮出，緝上便宜，詔以問中書令孫資，資以為有籌略，遂召拜騎都尉，遣參征蜀軍。

translations.literal: It happened Zhuge Liang came out; Ji submitted convenience proposals; the edict used it to ask Palace Secretariat Director Sun Zi; Zi thought he had stratagem and planning; thereupon summoned and appointed Colonel Commandant of Cavalry, dispatched him to join the army campaigning against Shu.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuge Liang invaded, he forwarded useful proposals; Sun Zi judged him a strategist, so the court named him colonel of cavalry and attached him to the Shu expedition.

sentences.zh: 軍罷，入為尚書郎，以稱職為明帝所識。

translations.literal: When the army dismissed, he entered as Gentleman of the Interior; because he was called competent he was noted by Emperor Ming.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign he became a gentleman of the interior; his efficiency caught Emperor Ming's eye.

sentences.zh: 帝以為緝之材能，多所堪任，試呼相工相之。

translations.literal: The emperor thought Ji's talents and abilities were many things he could bear; tried summoning a physiognomist to examine him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor believed him fit for many posts and secretly had a face-reader study him.

sentences.zh: 相者云：「不過二千石。

translations.literal: The physiognomist said: "Not more than two thousand shi."
translations.idiomatic: The diviner predicted he would rise no higher than a two-thousand-shi salary.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「何材如是而位止二千石乎？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "How can talent be thus yet position stop at two thousand shi?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming asked, "How can a man of such parts top out at two thousand shi?"

sentences.zh: 」及在東莞，領兵數千人。

translations.literal: When he was in Dongguan, he commanded several thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when Zhang Ji governed Dongguan he already led thousands of soldiers.

sentences.zh: 緝性吝於財而矜於勢，一旦以女徵去郡，還坐里舍，悒悒躁擾。

translations.literal: Ji's nature was stingy toward wealth yet proud of power; in one morning because of his daughter summoned he departed the commandery, returned and sat in village lodgings, depressed and restless.
translations.idiomatic: He was tight with money but vain of influence; the day his daughter's summons pulled him from his county, he sat brooding in a rented hovel, unable to settle.

sentences.zh: 數為國家陳擊吳、蜀形勢，又嘗對司馬大將軍料諸葛恪雖得勝於邊土，見誅不乆。

translations.literal: Several times for the state he laid out the situation of striking Wu and Shu, and once to General-in-chief Sima assessed Zhuge Ke: though he gained victory on the border lands, he would be executed before long.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly briefed the court on campaigns against Wu and Shu, and once told Sima Shi that Zhuge Ke, for all his frontier victories, would soon lose his head.

sentences.zh: 大將軍問其故，緝云：「威震其主，功蓋一國，欲不死可得乎？

translations.literal: The general-in-chief asked the reason; Ji said: "His awesomeness shakes his lord; merit covers one state—wishing not to die, can it be obtained?"
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, he answered, "His prestige overshadows his sovereign and his deeds swallow the state—how could he hope to live?"

sentences.zh: 」及恪從合肥還，吳果殺之。

translations.literal: When Ke returned from Hefei, Wu indeed killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuge Ke returned from Hefei, Wu executed him as predicted.

sentences.zh: 大將軍聞恪死，謂衆人曰：「諸葛恪多輩耳！

translations.literal: The general-in-chief heard Ke died and said to the crowd: "Zhuge Ke was a mere mediocrity!
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi exclaimed, "Zhuge Ke was nothing but a mediocrity!

sentences.zh: 近張敬仲縣論恪，以為必見殺，今果然如此。

translations.literal: Recently Zhang Jingzhong in conversation assessed Ke, thinking he would surely be seen killed; now indeed it was thus."
translations.idiomatic: Only the other day Zhang Jingzhong told me Ke would die for it—and so he has."

sentences.zh: 敬仲之智為勝恪也。

translations.literal: Jingzhong's wisdom surpassed Ke's.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji's foresight outclassed Zhuge Ke's.

sentences.zh: 」緝與李豐通家，又居相側近。

translations.literal: Ji was connected by marriage with Li Feng and also dwelled near the minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was kin by marriage to Li Feng and lived next door to the chief minister.

sentences.zh: 豐時取急出，子藐往見之，有所咨道。

translations.literal: Feng at the time took urgent business and went out; his son Miao went to see him, having something to consult and convey.
translations.idiomatic: Once Li Feng left on sudden business; his son Li Miao dropped in on Zhang Ji for advice.

sentences.zh: 豐被收，事與緝連，遂收送廷尉，賜死獄中，其諸子皆並誅。

translations.literal: Feng was arrested; the affair connected with Ji; thereupon he was seized and delivered to the Minister of Justice, granted death in prison; his various sons were all together executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Feng fell, Zhang Ji was implicated, sent to the minister of justice, strangled in jail, and his sons were put to death with him.

sentences.zh: 緝孫殷，晉永興中為梁州刺史，見《晉書》。〉

translations.literal: Ji's grandson Yin, in the Yongxing period of Jin was Inspector of Liangzhou; see the Jin shu.〉
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Zhang Yin became Jin's Liangzhou inspector in the Yongxing era—the Jin shu carries his biography.〉

sentences.zh: 溫恢字曼基，太原祁人也。

translations.literal: Wen Hui, courtesy name Manji, was a native of Qi in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Hui, style Manji, came from Qi in Taiyuan commandery.

sentences.zh: 父恕，爲涿郡太守，卒。

translations.literal: His father Shu was Administrator of Zhuo commandery and died.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wen Shu had been prefect of Zhuo and died in office.

sentences.zh: 恢年十五，送丧還歸鄉里，内足於財。

translations.literal: At age fifteen Hui escorted the funeral and returned to his village home, inwardly sufficient in wealth.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen Wen Hui brought his father's coffin home and found himself heir to a considerable fortune.

sentences.zh: 恢曰：「世方亂，安以富爲？

translations.literal: Hui said: "The age is about to be in chaos—how can one take wealth as sufficient?"
translations.idiomatic: He said, "The world is sliding into chaos—what good is money hoarded in a jar?"

sentences.zh: 」一朝尽散，振施宗族。

translations.literal: In one morning he entirely scattered it, extending relief to the clan.
translations.idiomatic: In a single morning he gave it away to clansmen in need.

sentences.zh: 州里高之，比之郇越。

translations.literal: The commandery and village esteemed him, comparing him to Xun Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors ranked him with the ancient paragon Xun Yue.

sentences.zh: 舉孝廉，爲廪丘長，鄢陵、廣川令，彭城、鲁相，所在見稱。

translations.literal: Recommended Filial and Incorrupt, he became chief of Linqiu, magistrate of Yanling and Guangchuan, chancellor of Pengcheng and Lu; wherever he went he was praised.
translations.idiomatic: Nominated filial and incorrupt, he served as chief of Linqiu, magistrate of Yanling and Guangchuan, and chancellor of Pengcheng and Lu, winning praise at every post.

sentences.zh: 入爲丞相主簿，出爲扬州刺史。

translations.literal: He entered as chief clerk to the chancellor, went out as Inspector of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the chancellor's secretariat, then sent out as Yangzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「甚欲使卿在親近，顾以爲不如此州事大。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor said: "I greatly wish to have you at intimate closeness, yet I think not like this—affairs of the province are great.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao told him, "I would gladly keep you at my elbow, but Yangzhou matters more right now.

sentences.zh: 故書云：‘股肱良哉！

translations.literal: Therefore the document says: "Are not the thighs and arms good!"
translations.idiomatic: The old text says, "Sturdy are the arms and legs!"

sentences.zh: 庶事康哉！

translations.literal: The hundred tasks are well!"
translations.idiomatic: "Then every task runs smoothly!"

sentences.zh: ’得無當得蒋济爲治中邪？

translations.literal: Is it not fitting that Jiang Ji ought to be obtained as chief clerk?"
translations.idiomatic: Would not Jiang Ji suit you as chief clerk?"

sentences.zh: 」時济見爲丹杨太守，乃遣济還州。

translations.literal: At the time Ji was seen as Administrator of Danyang; thereupon he dispatched Ji back to the province.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ji was then prefect of Danyang; Cao Cao ordered him back to Yangzhou as Wen Hui's deputy.

sentences.zh: 又语張辽、乐進等曰：「扬州刺史晓達軍事，動静與共咨議。」

translations.literal: He also spoke to Zhang Liao, Yue Jin, and others saying: "The Inspector of Yangzhou is clear through military affairs; in movement and stillness together consult with him."
translations.idiomatic: He instructed Zhang Liao, Yue Jin, and the other generals, "The Yangzhou inspector knows war—take him into counsel on every move."

sentences.zh: 建安二十四年，孫权攻合肥，是時諸州皆屯戍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Jian'an, Sun Quan attacked Hefei; at this time the various provinces all stationed garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 24 Sun Quan struck at Hefei while every province kept troops in the field.

sentences.zh: 恢謂兗州刺史裴潜曰：「此間雖有贼，不足憂，而畏征南方有變。

translations.literal: Hui said to Inspector of Yanzhou Pei Qian: "Here though there are bandits, it is not worth worry; what is feared is change in the south on the expedition.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Hui told Yanzhou inspector Pei Qian, "Bandits here are nothing; I fear trouble on the southern front.

sentences.zh: 今水生而子孝縣軍，無有远備。

translations.literal: Now the waters have risen yet Zixiao isolates the army without distant preparation."
translations.idiomatic: The rivers are high and Cao Ren has left his army exposed without a deep defense."

sentences.zh: 關羽骁锐，乘利而進，必將爲患。

translations.literal: Guan Yu is fierce and sharp; riding profit he will advance—he is sure to become a trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu is swift and aggressive; he will seize the moment and become a real threat."

sentences.zh: 」於是有樊城之事。

translations.literal: Thereupon there was the Fancheng affair.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward came the siege of Fancheng.

sentences.zh: 詔書召潜及豫州刺史呂贡等，潜等缓之。

translations.literal: An edict summoned Qian and Inspector of Yu Province Lu Gong and others; Qian and others delayed it.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial messengers summoned Pei Qian and Yu inspector Lu Gong, but they dragged their feet.

sentences.zh: 恢密语潜曰：「此必襄陽之急欲赴之也。

translations.literal: Hui secretly spoke to Qian saying: "This surely is the urgency of Xiangyang wishing to hurry there."
translations.idiomatic: Wen Hui whispered to Pei Qian, "This can only mean Xiangyang is in crisis."

sentences.zh: 所以不爲急會者，不欲惊動远眾。

translations.literal: The reason it is not an urgent assembly is that they do not wish to alarm and move the distant masses.
translations.idiomatic: They avoid a general mobilization so as not to panic the whole realm.

sentences.zh: 一二日必有密書促卿進道，張辽等又將被召。

translations.literal: In one or two days there is sure to be a secret letter urging you to advance on the road; Zhang Liao and others again will be summoned."
translations.idiomatic: Within a day or two sealed orders will rush you forward, and Zhang Liao will be called in as well."

sentences.zh: 辽等素知王意，後召前至，卿受其责矣！

translations.literal: Liao and others always know the king's intention; afterward when summoned you arrive first—you will receive their blame!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liao and the rest know how the king thinks; if you drag your feet until they are called in first, you will bear the blame yourself!"

sentences.zh: 」潜受其言，置辎重，更爲轻装速发，果被促令。

translations.literal: Qian received his words, set aside baggage trains, again made light dress for rapid departure, indeed received urgent orders.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Qian took the hint, shed his heavy baggage, switched to light gear, and galloped off—just as sealed orders arrived to hurry him forward.

sentences.zh: 辽等寻各見召，如恢所策。

translations.literal: Liao and others soon each were summoned, as Hui had calculated.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liao and the others were each recalled soon after, exactly as Wen Hui had predicted.

sentences.zh: 文帝践阼，以恢爲侍中，出爲魏郡太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen ascended the throne, he made Hui palace attendant, went out as Administrator of Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Pi took the throne he named Wen Hui palace attendant, then sent him out as prefect of Wei commandery.

sentences.zh: 數年，遷凉州刺史，持节领护羌校尉。

translations.literal: After several years he was transferred Inspector of Liangzhou, bearing credentials and concurrently Colonel Who Protects the Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: A few years later he became Liangzhou inspector, baton in hand, with concurrent appointment as protector of the Qiang.

sentences.zh: 道病卒，時年四十五。

translations.literal: On the road he died of illness, at the time age forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died of an illness on the march at forty-five.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「恢有柱石之質，服事先帝，功勤明著。

translations.literal: The edict said: "Hui had the substance of a pillar and stone, served the late emperor, merit and diligence manifestly clear.
translations.idiomatic: An edict mourned him: "Wen Hui had the mettle of a pillar; he served my late father with conspicuous zeal.

sentences.zh: 及爲朕執事，忠於王室，故授之以萬里之任，任之以一方之事。

translations.literal: When he held office for Us, was loyal to the royal house, therefore We conferred on him the commission of ten thousand li, entrusted him with the affairs of one quarter."
translations.idiomatic: In my own service he proved utterly loyal, which is why I gave him a frontier stretching ten thousand li."

sentences.zh: 如何不遂，吾甚愍之！

translations.literal: How could it not be fulfilled—We greatly pity him!"
translations.idiomatic: That promise was cut short—how deeply I grieve!"

sentences.zh: 」赐恢子生爵關内侯。

translations.literal: He granted Hui's son Sheng noble rank as Neighbourhood Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He enfeoffed Wen Hui's son Wen Sheng as a neighborhood marquis.

sentences.zh: 生早卒，爵絕。

translations.literal: Sheng died early; the noble rank was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Sheng died young and the title lapsed.

sentences.zh: 恢卒後，汝南孟建爲凉州刺史，有治名，官至征東將軍。

translations.literal: After Hui died, Meng Jian of Runan became Inspector of Liangzhou, had a reputation for good order, his office reached General Who Conquers the East.
translations.idiomatic: After Wen Hui's death Meng Jian of Runan succeeded him in Liangzhou with a strong record and rose to general who conquers the east.

sentences.zh: 〈魏略曰：建字公威，少與諸葛亮俱游學。

translations.literal: The Wei lue says: Jian's courtesy name was Gongwei; in youth he studied abroad together with Zhuge Liang.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei lue gives Meng Jian, style Gongwei, as Zhuge Liang's fellow student in their wandering years.

sentences.zh: 亮後出祁山，答司馬宣王書，使杜子绪宣意於公威也。〉

translations.literal: Later when Liang came out at Qishan, answering Sima Yi's letter, he had Du Zixu convey his mind to Gongwei.〉
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuge Liang marched to Qishan he sent Du Zixu to carry his greetings to Meng Jian in a letter answering Sima Yi.〉

sentences.zh: 贾逵字梁道，河東襄陵人也。

translations.literal: Jia Kui, courtesy name Liangdao, was a native of Xiangling in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kui, style Liangdao, was a man of Xiangling in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 自爲兒童，戏弄常設部伍，祖父習異之，曰：「汝大必爲將率。

translations.literal: From the time he was a child, in play he always arranged troops in formation; his grandfather Xi marveled at him and said: "You grown up will surely be a general or leader."
translations.idiomatic: Even as a boy he lined up playmates like soldiers; his grandfather Jia Xi said, "This child will command armies."

sentences.zh: 」口授兵法數萬言。

translations.literal: Orally he taught him military writings numbering tens of thousands of characters.
translations.idiomatic: The old man drilled him in tens of thousands of characters of military classics by rote.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：逵世爲著姓，少孤家贫，冬常無袴，过其妻兄柳孚宿，其明無何，著孚袴去，故時人謂之通健。〉

translations.literal: The Wei lue says: For generations Kui's clan was a prominent surname; in youth he was orphaned and the family was poor; in winter he often lacked trousers; passing his wife's elder brother Liu Fu's to lodge for the night, the next morning without ado he put on Fu's trousers and left; therefore people of the time called him unrestrained and hardy.〉
translations.idiomatic: The Wei lue adds that the Jias were a great clan fallen on hard times: one winter the boy had no pants, spent the night with his brother-in-law Liu Fu, walked off in Liu Fu's breeches at dawn, and earned a reputation for brazen toughness.〉

sentences.zh: 初爲郡吏，守绛邑長。

translations.literal: At first he was a commandery clerk, guarding as chief of Jiangyi.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a county clerk and acting chief of Jiangyi.

sentences.zh: 郭援之攻河東，所經城邑皆下，逵坚守，援攻之不拔，乃召单于並軍急攻之。

translations.literal: When Guo Yuan attacked Hedong, every city and town he passed fell; Kui firmly defended; Yuan attacked him but could not take him, thereupon summoned the Shanyu and combined armies urgently to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yuan's sweep through Hedong took every town until he reached Jia Kui's walls; unable to storm them, Guo Yuan called in the Xiongnu chanyu for a joint assault.

sentences.zh: 城將溃，绛父老與援要，不害逵。

translations.literal: The city was about to collapse; the elders of Jiang made a pact with Yuan not to harm Kui.
translations.idiomatic: As the walls began to give, the Jiang elders bargained with Guo Yuan to spare their magistrate.

sentences.zh: 绛人既溃，援聞逵名，欲使爲將，以兵劫之，逵不動。

translations.literal: The people of Jiang having broken, Yuan heard Kui's name and wished to make him a general, used troops to coerce him, but Kui did not move.
translations.idiomatic: When the town fell, Guo Yuan, impressed by Jia Kui's name, tried to press him into service at sword point; Jia Kui did not stir.

sentences.zh: 左右引逵使叩头，逵叱之曰：「安有國家長吏爲贼叩头！

translations.literal: Those at his sides pulled Kui to make him knock his head; Kui rebuked them saying: "How can there be a senior officer of the state who for bandits knocks his head!"
translations.idiomatic: Guards tried to force him to kowtow; he snarled, "No magistrate of the Han kneels to rebels!"

sentences.zh: 」援怒，將斩之。

translations.literal: Yuan was angry and was about to behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yuan flew into a rage and ordered his execution.

sentences.zh: 绛吏民聞將杀逵，皆乘城呼曰：「負要杀我賢君，宁俱死耳！

translations.literal: The clerks and commoners of Jiang heard he was about to kill Kui, all mounted the walls and shouted: "Violating the pact to kill our worthy lord—we would rather all die!"
translations.idiomatic: The townsfolk swarmed the ramparts shouting, "Break your oath and you kill our good magistrate—we die with him!"

sentences.zh: 」左右義逵，多爲请，遂得免。

translations.literal: Those at his sides admired Kui and for the most part pleaded; thereupon he obtained release.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yuan's officers, moved by Jia Kui's courage, pleaded until his life was spared.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：援捕得逵，逵不肯拜，謂援曰：「王府君临郡积年，不知足下曷爲者也？

translations.literal: The Wei lue says: When Yuan captured Kui, Kui refused to bow and said to Yuan: "Lord Wang has governed the commandery for accumulated years—do I know who you are?"
translations.idiomatic: The Wei lue quotes him telling Guo Yuan, "Prefect Wang has ruled this county for years—who exactly are you?"

sentences.zh: 」援怒曰：「促斩之。

translations.literal: Yuan angrily said: "Hasten to behead him."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yuan roared, "Kill him at once."

sentences.zh: 」諸將覆护，乃囚於壶關，闭著土窖中，以车轮盖上，使人固守。

translations.literal: The various generals covered and protected him, thereupon imprisoned him in Huguan, closed him in an earthen pit, covered it with cart wheels, and had men firmly guard.
translations.idiomatic: His own officers shielded him; Guo Yuan had Jia Kui flung into an earthen cell at Huguan, roofed with cart wheels and heavily guarded.

sentences.zh: 方將杀之，逵從窖中謂守者曰：「此間無健兒邪，而當使義士死此中乎？

translations.literal: Just as he was about to kill him, Kui from inside the pit said to the guards: "Is there no brave lad here, yet you would let a righteous knight die in this place?"
translations.idiomatic: As the executioner approached, Jia Kui shouted into the pit, "Is there no man of spirit left who would let a loyal officer rot here?"

sentences.zh: 」時有祝公道者，與逵非故人，而適聞其言，怜其守正危厄，乃夜盗往引出，折械遣去，不语其姓名。〉

translations.literal: At the time there was one Zhu Gongdao, not an old acquaintance of Kui, who happened to hear his words, pitied him for keeping integrity in peril, and therefore by night stole in, led him out, broke his fetters and sent him off, not telling his name.〉
translations.idiomatic: A stranger named Zhu Gongdao overheard, pitied his integrity, slipped in by night, freed him, broke his chains, and vanished without giving his name.〉

sentences.zh: 初，逵过皮氏，曰：「爭地先据者胜。

translations.literal: At first, when Kui passed Pishi, he said: "In fighting for ground, he who first occupies it wins."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, passing Pishi, Jia Kui had said, "In a contest for terrain, the side that seizes the ground first wins."

sentences.zh: 」及圍怎，知不免，乃使人間行送印绶歸郡，且曰「急据皮氏」。

translations.literal: When the siege [怎, text] pressed, knowing he could not escape, he thereupon had someone by secret route send the seal-cord back to the commandery, and said "urgently occupy Pishi."
translations.idiomatic: When the siege turned desperate and capture seemed certain, he smuggled his official seal back to headquarters with orders to seize Pishi before the enemy could.

sentences.zh: 援既並绛眾，將進兵。

translations.literal: Yuan having combined the masses of Jiang, was about to advance troops.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yuan absorbed the Jiang garrison and prepared to march on.

sentences.zh: 逵恐其先得皮氏，乃以他计疑援谋人祝奥，援由是留七日。

translations.literal: Kui feared he would first obtain Pishi, thereupon with another stratagem made Yuan's adviser Zhu Ao suspicious; Yuan for this reason delayed seven days.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Guo Yuan would reach Pishi first, Jia Kui spread disinformation through Guo's adviser Zhu Ao and pinned him down for seven days.

sentences.zh: 郡從逵言，故得無敗。

translations.literal: The commandery followed Kui's words, therefore was able not to be defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery obeyed his warning and held the critical ground.

sentences.zh: 〈《孫资别傳》曰：资舉河東计吏，到许，荐於相府曰：「逵在绛邑，帅厉吏民，與贼郭援交戰，力尽而敗，爲贼所俘，挺然直志，颜辭不屈；

translations.literal: The Sun Zi bie zhuan says: When Zi was recommended as Hedong clerk of accounts and arrived at Xu, he recommended to the chancellery saying: "Kui in Jiangyi led and encouraged clerks and commoners, battled with the bandit Guo Yuan, strength exhausted then was defeated, was captured by the bandits, stood straight with firm intent, his words and countenance did not bend;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zi's supplementary biography records his memorial: "At Jiangyi Jia Kui rallied clerks and townsmen against Guo Yuan, fought until overwhelmed, fell captive, yet stood unbent;

sentences.zh: 忠言聞於大眾，烈节显於當時，雖古之直发、据鼎，罔以加也。

translations.literal: loyal words heard among the great crowd, fierce integrity displayed in that moment—though the ancient who bared his hair and grasped the cauldron could not surpass it.
translations.idiomatic: his defiance rang through the army—no ancient martyr who seized the sacrificial cauldron could surpass him.

sentences.zh: 其才兼文武，誠時之利用。

translations.literal: His talent combines civil and military—truly timely usefulness."
translations.idiomatic: He unites civil and military gifts—exactly the man the times require."

sentences.zh: 」魏略曰：郭援破後，逵乃知前出己者爲祝公道。

translations.literal: The Wei lue says: After Guo Yuan was defeated, Kui then knew the one who earlier had led him out was Zhu Gongdao.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei lue notes that only after Guo Yuan's defeat did Jia Kui learn his rescuer had been Zhu Gongdao.

sentences.zh: 公道，河南人也。

translations.literal: Gongdao was a man of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Gongdao came from Henan.

sentences.zh: 後坐他事，當伏法。

translations.literal: Later because of another affair he was to suffer capital punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Later he faced execution on another charge.

sentences.zh: 逵救之，力不能解，爲之改服焉。〉

translations.literal: Kui sought to save him, strength could not resolve it, for him changed garb.〉
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kui tried to save him but could not; he mourned in changed robes.〉

sentences.zh: 後舉茂才，除渑池令。

translations.literal: Later he was recommended Outstanding Talent, appointed magistrate of Mianchi.
translations.idiomatic: He was later nominated for outstanding talent and made magistrate of Mianchi.

sentences.zh: 高幹之反，張琰將舉兵以应之。

translations.literal: When Gao Gan rebelled, Zhang Yan was about to raise troops to respond to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Gan rose, Zhang Yan of Mianchi prepared to join the revolt.

sentences.zh: 逵不知其谋，往見琰。

translations.literal: Kui did not know his plot and went to see Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kui, unaware of the plot, called on Zhang Yan.

sentences.zh: 聞變起，欲還，恐見執，乃爲琰画计，如與同谋者，琰信之。

translations.literal: Hearing the mutiny had begun, he wished to return, feared being seized, therefore for Yan drew up plans as if he were a fellow conspirator, and Yan trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of the uprising, he dared not flee openly; instead he feigned collusion, drafted plans for Zhang Yan, and won his confidence.

sentences.zh: 時縣寄治蠡城，城堑不固，逵從琰求兵脩城。

translations.literal: At the time the county was provisionally administered from Licheng; the city moats were not solid; Kui from Yan requested troops to repair the walls.
translations.idiomatic: The county seat had been shifted to Licheng with weak walls; Jia Kui asked Zhang Yan for laborers to strengthen them.

sentences.zh: 諸欲爲亂者皆不隐其谋，故逵得尽诛之。

translations.literal: Those who wished to make rebellion all did not hide their plots, therefore Kui was able entirely to execute them.
translations.idiomatic: Would-be rebels exposed their scheme in the work parties, and Jia Kui had them all put to death.

sentences.zh: 遂脩城拒琰。

translations.literal: Thereupon he repaired the walls and resisted Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He then refortified Licheng against Zhang Yan.

sentences.zh: 琰敗，逵以丧祖父去官，司徒辟爲掾，以議郎参司隶軍事。

translations.literal: When Yan was defeated, Kui because of mourning for his grandfather left office; the Minister of Education summoned him as a clerk, as Consultant Counselor joined the metropolitan army staff.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Yan fell, Jia Kui resigned to mourn his grandfather, was recalled to the ministry of education, then served as consultant on the metropolitan command staff.

sentences.zh: 太祖征馬超，至弘农，曰「此西道之要」，以逵领弘农太守。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor campaigned against Ma Chao, reaching Hongnong, said "this is the key to the western road," he had Kui concurrently act as Administrator of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao marched against Ma Chao he stopped at Hongnong, called it the linchpin of the western road, and named Jia Kui acting prefect.

sentences.zh: 召見计事，大悦之，謂左右曰：「使天下二千石悉如贾逵，吾何憂？

translations.literal: He summoned him to discuss planning, greatly delighted in him, said to those at his sides: "If every two-thousand-shi in the realm were like Jia Kui, what would I worry about?"
translations.idiomatic: He was so pleased with Jia Kui's counsel that he said, "If every magistrate were like Jia Kui, I would sleep soundly."

sentences.zh: 」其後发兵，逵疑屯田都尉藏亡民。

translations.literal: Afterward when issuing troops, Kui suspected the agricultural colony commandant was hiding fugitive commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Later, mobilizing supplies, Jia Kui suspected the colony commandant of harboring runaway peasants.

sentences.zh: 都尉自以不屬郡，言语不顺。

translations.literal: The commandant considered himself not subordinate to the commandery; his words were not compliant.
translations.idiomatic: The commandant insisted he reported to the capital, not to the prefect, and answered insolently.

sentences.zh: 逵怒，收之，數以罪，挝折脚，坐免。

translations.literal: Kui was angry, seized him, enumerated his crimes, beat and broke his foot, and by sitting was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kui had him arrested, listed his offenses, beat him until his leg broke, and lost his own post for excessive force.

sentences.zh: 然太祖心善逵，以爲丞相主簿。

translations.literal: Yet the Grand Progenitor inwardly approved Kui and made him chief clerk to the chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao nevertheless valued his zeal and appointed him chief clerk of the chancellor.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：太祖欲征吳而大霖雨，三軍多不原行。

translations.literal: The Wei lue says: The Grand Progenitor wished to campaign against Wu but great rains fell; the three armies for the most part did not wish to march.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei lue tells how Cao Cao meant to strike Wu but torrential rains left the army unwilling to march.

sentences.zh: 太祖知其然，恐外有谏者，教曰：「今孤戒严，未知所之，有谏者死。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor knew it was so, feared there would be remonstrators outside, ordered saying: "Now I, alone, am under arms and do not yet know where I shall go—whoever remonstrates dies."
translations.idiomatic: Knowing their mood, he forbade debate on pain of death: "I am mobilized and my target is secret—advise me and you die."

sentences.zh: 」逵受教，謂其同寮三主簿曰：「今實不可出，而教如此，不可不谏也。

translations.literal: Kui received the order and said to his three fellow chief clerks: "Now in truth we cannot go out, yet the order is thus—we cannot fail to remonstrate."
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kui told his fellow chief clerks, "This expedition is folly, yet the order forbids counsel—we must speak anyway."

sentences.zh: 」乃建谏草以示三人，三人不获已，皆署名，入白事。

translations.literal: Thereupon he drafted a remonstrance memorandum to show the three men; the three had no choice, all signed names, and entered to report the affair.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted a memorial and bullied the three into cosigning it.

sentences.zh: 太祖怒，收逵等。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor was angry and seized Kui and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao arrested all four.

sentences.zh: 當送狱，取造意者，逵即言「我造意」，遂走詣狱。

translations.literal: When about to send them to prison, seeking the one who originated the idea, Kui immediately said "I originated the idea," thereupon ran off to prison.
translations.idiomatic: Asked who had started the protest, Jia Kui cried, "I did," and bolted for the jail himself.

sentences.zh: 狱吏以逵主簿也，不即著械。

translations.literal: The jail clerk because Kui was chief clerk did not immediately put fetters on him.
translations.idiomatic: The warden hesitated to shackle a chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 謂狱吏曰：「促械我。

translations.literal: He said to the jail clerk: "Hasten to fetter me.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kui snapped, "Shackle me now.

sentences.zh: 尊者且疑我在近职，求缓於卿，今將遣人来察我。

translations.literal: The honored one will suspect I hold a nearby post and seek leniency from you; now he will send someone to inspect me."
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor will think I am trading on my office to win favors—he is about to send a spy."

sentences.zh: 」逵著械適讫，而太祖果遣家中人就狱视逵。

translations.literal: Kui having put on fetters just finished, and the Grand Progenitor indeed dispatched a household man to go to prison and observe Kui.
translations.idiomatic: The fetters had barely clicked when a household agent arrived to inspect him.

sentences.zh: 既而教曰：「逵無恶意，原復其职。

translations.literal: Afterward he ordered saying: "Kui had no evil intent; pardon and restore his office."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao then relented: "Jia Kui meant no harm—restore him."

sentences.zh: 」始，逵爲諸生，略览大義，取其可用。

translations.literal: At first, when Kui was a student, he broadly perused the great meaning and took what was usable.
translations.idiomatic: As a student he skimmed the classics for whatever served statecraft.

sentences.zh: 最好春秋左傳，及爲牧守，常自课读之，月常一遍。

translations.literal: He most loved the Zuo zhuan of the Chunqiu; when he became a shepherd guardian he always set himself lessons to read it, monthly often one complete pass.
translations.idiomatic: He loved the Zuo commentary best; as a governor he reread it cover to cover every month.

sentences.zh: 逵前在弘农，與典农校尉爭公事，不得理，乃发愤生瘿，後所病稍大，自启原欲令医割之。

translations.literal: Formerly when Kui was in Hongnong he disputed public business with the agricultural colony commandant, did not obtain justice, therefore in anger developed a goiter; afterward the ailment gradually grew larger; he personally petitioned wishing to have a physician cut it.
translations.idiomatic: A losing argument with the colony commandant in Hongnong had left him with a goiter that swelled until he begged permission to have it cut out.

sentences.zh: 太祖惜逵忠，恐其不活，教「謝主簿，吾聞‘十人割瘿九人死’」。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor treasured Kui's loyalty, feared he would not survive, ordered "tell Chief Clerk Jia—I have heard 'of ten men who cut a goiter, nine die.'"
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao, cherishing his loyalty, sent word: "Tell the chief clerk they say nine of ten who cut a wen die."

sentences.zh: 逵猶行其意，而瘿愈大。

translations.literal: Kui still carried out his intent, and the goiter grew larger.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kui insisted on surgery in any case, and the growth only worsened.

sentences.zh: 逵本名衢，後改爲逵。〉

translations.literal: Kui's original name was Qu; afterward changed to Kui.〉
translations.idiomatic: His birth name had been Jia Qu; he later adopted the name Kui.〉

sentences.zh: 太祖征刘備，先遣逵至斜谷觀形勢。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor campaigned against Liu Bei, he first dispatched Kui to Xie Valley to observe the situation.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against Liu Bei he sent Jia Kui ahead to scout Xie Valley.

sentences.zh: 道逢水衡，载囚人數十车，逵以軍事急，辄竟重者一人，皆放其餘。

translations.literal: On the road he encountered a Shuiheng [convoy], carrying several tens of cartloads of prisoners; Kui because military affairs were urgent thereupon judged the heaviest of one man, all releasing the rest.
translations.idiomatic: He met a government convoy—the text reads "Shuiheng"—with dozens of carts of prisoners; citing military urgency he retried one capital case and released the rest.

sentences.zh: 太祖善之，拜谏議大夫，與夏侯尚並掌軍计。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor approved him, appointed Grandee Remonstrant, together with Xiahou Shang jointly managed military planning.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao approved, named him grandee remonstrant, and paired him with Xiahou Shang on operational planning.

sentences.zh: 太祖崩洛陽，逵典丧事。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor died at Luoyang, Kui directed funeral affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao died at Luoyang, Jia Kui directed the obsequies.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：時太子在鄴，鄢陵侯未到，士民颇苦劳役，又有疾疠，於是軍中骚動。

translations.literal: The Wei lue says: At the time the heir-apparent was at Ye, the Marquis of Yanling had not yet arrived, officers and commoners suffered corvée and there was also pestilence, therefore the army was restless.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei lue records that the heir was still at Ye, Cao Zhang had not arrived, corvée and plague had frayed morale, and the camp seethed with rumor.

sentences.zh: 羣寮恐天下有變，欲不发丧。

translations.literal: The host of officials feared there would be change in the realm and wished not to issue mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Some ministers urged suppressing news of the death lest the realm revolt.

sentences.zh: 逵建議爲不可秘，乃发哀，令内外皆入临，临讫，各安叙不得動。

translations.literal: Kui proposed that it could not be kept secret; thereupon they issued mourning, ordered inner and outer all to enter mourning audience; when mourning audience finished, each settled in order and was not allowed to move.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kui insisted on a public proclamation, staged the formal lament, then locked the camp in place until order returned.

sentences.zh: 而青州軍擅击鼓相引去。

translations.literal: But the Qingzhou army on its own struck drums and mutually led one another away.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Qingzhou corps beat their drums and marched off on their own.

sentences.zh: 眾人以爲宜禁止之，不從者讨之。

translations.literal: The crowd thought it fitting to prohibit them; those who did not obey were to be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Counselors wanted to hunt them down as deserters.

sentences.zh: 逵以爲「方大丧在殡，嗣王未立，宜因而抚之」。

translations.literal: Kui thought "just now great mourning is in the coffin hall, the successor king is not yet established—it is fitting thereby to soothe them."
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kui argued that with the succession still unsettled they should coax the men back, not provoke them.

sentences.zh: 乃爲作長檄，告所在给其廪食。〉

translations.literal: Thereupon for them he drafted a long proclamation, informing each place to give them granary food.〉
translations.idiomatic: He drafted a long manifesto promising rations at every post along their route.〉

sentences.zh: 時鄢陵侯彰行越骑將軍，從長安来赴，問逵先王玺绶所在。

translations.literal: At the time Marquis of Yanling Cao Zhang acted as General of Agile Cavalry on the Left, coming from Chang'an to attend; he asked Kui where the late king's seal-cord was.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhang galloped in from Chang'an as acting general of agile cavalry and demanded where the late king's seals were kept.

sentences.zh: 逵正色曰：「太子在鄴，國有储副。

translations.literal: Kui with stern countenance said: "The heir-apparent is at Ye; the state has a stored successor.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kui answered coldly, "The heir is at Ye; the succession is already fixed.

sentences.zh: 先王玺绶，非君侯所宜問也。

translations.literal: The late king's seal-cord is not what you, lord, ought to inquire about."
translations.idiomatic: The late king's seals are no business of yours, my lord."

sentences.zh: 」遂奉梓宫還鄴。

translations.literal: Thereupon he escorted the catalpa coffin back to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He then convoyed the catafalque to Ye.

sentences.zh: 文帝即王位，以鄴縣户數萬在都下，多不法，乃以逵爲鄴令。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen assumed the king's throne, because Ye county had households numbering ten thousand under the capital and many were not law-abiding, he therefore made Kui magistrate of Ye.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Pi became king, Ye county—tens of thousands of households under the capital's shadow—was rife with crime, so he named Jia Kui magistrate.

sentences.zh: 月餘，遷魏郡太守。

translations.literal: After more than a month he was promoted Administrator of Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month he rose to prefect of Wei commandery.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：初，魏郡官屬颇以公事期會有所急切，會聞逵當爲郡，舉府皆詣縣門外。

translations.literal: The Wei lue says: At first the officials of Wei commandery because of public business meetings had something urgently pressing; when they heard Kui was about to become the commandery head, the whole bureau went to the county gate outside.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei lue tells how the Wei commandery staff, dreading overdue accounts, massed outside the county gate the day his appointment arrived.

sentences.zh: 及遷書到，逵出門，而郡官屬悉當門，謁逵於车下。

translations.literal: When the transfer document arrived, Kui went out the gate, and the commandery officials all blocked the gate, paying respects to Kui beneath his cart.
translations.idiomatic: When Jia Kui emerged they mobbed his carriage for obeisance.

sentences.zh: 逵抵掌曰：「詣治所，何宜如是！」〉

translations.literal: Kui clapped palms and said: "Go to the administration—how should it be thus!"〉
translations.idiomatic: He clapped his hands and barked, "Your office is in the yamen—not in my dust!"〉

sentences.zh: 大軍出征，復爲丞相主簿祭酒。

translations.literal: When the great army campaigned, he again became chief clerk to the chancellor and libationer.
translations.idiomatic: On the next great expedition he resumed chief clerk and chancellor's libationer.

sentences.zh: 逵尝坐人爲罪，王曰：「叔向猶十世宥之，况逵功德親在其身乎？

translations.literal: Kui once sat because another person was guilty; the king said: "Shu Xiang still pardoned ten generations—how much more Kui whose merit and virtue are personally on him?"
translations.idiomatic: When a subordinate's crime touched him, Cao Pi said, "Shu Xiang pardoned ten generations of kin—shall I be harsher on Jia Kui himself?"

sentences.zh: 」從至黎陽，津渡者亂行，逵斩之，乃整。
