translations.literal: Following to Liyang, those crossing the ford moved in disorderly lines; Kui beheaded them, then it was orderly.
translations.idiomatic: At the Liyang crossing he restored order by beheading rioters.

sentences.zh: 至谯，以逵爲豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Reaching Qiao, he made Kui Inspector of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: At Qiao he named him Yu inspector.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：逵爲豫州。

translations.literal: The Wei lue says: When Kui became Inspector of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei lue, on his appointment as inspector of Yu Province, records:

sentences.zh: 逵進曰：「臣守天門，出入六年，天門始開，而臣在外。

translations.literal: Kui advanced saying: "Your subject guards the Gate of Heaven; going out and entering six years, the Gate of Heaven just opens, yet Your subject is outside."
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kui protested, "Six years I have guarded your northern gate; now it opens to your progress and I am left outside the capital."

sentences.zh: 唯殿下爲兆民计，無违天人之望。」〉

translations.literal: Only may Your Highness plan for the myriad people—do not go against the expectation of Heaven and the people."〉
translations.idiomatic: I beg you, my lord, to act for the people of the realm and not disappoint what Heaven and men expect of you."〉

sentences.zh: 是時天下初復，州郡多不摄。

translations.literal: At this time the realm had just been restored; provinces and commanderies for the most part did not hold together.
translations.idiomatic: The empire was only beginning to knit together again, and most provincial governments were still slack.

sentences.zh: 逵曰：「州本以御史出監諸郡，以六条詔書察長吏二千石已下，故其狀皆言严能鹰扬有督察之才，不言安静寬仁有恺悌之德也。

translations.literal: Kui said: "Provinces were originally because censors went out to supervise the various commanderies, with the six-clause edict inspecting senior officials from two-thousand-shi downward; therefore their reports all spoke of stern capability, eagle-soaring, having talent for inspection and supervision, and did not speak of quiet calm, lenient benevolence, having the virtue of gentle kindness."
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kui explained, "Inspectors were meant to be the emperor's eyes—empowered by the six statutes to watch every magistrate below two-thousand-shi rank—so their reports praised hawks who terrorized local officials, never men known for mercy or ease."

sentences.zh: 今長吏慢法，盗贼公行，州知而不纠，天下復何取正乎？

translations.literal: Now senior officials treat the law lightly, bandits and robbers move in the open, the province knows yet does not correct—what is the realm again to take as standard?"
translations.idiomatic: Today magistrates flout the law, brigands walk the roads, and the provincial office looks the other way—where then is the standard for the world?"

sentences.zh: 」兵曹從事受前刺史假，逵到官數月，乃還；

translations.literal: The military bureau clerk had received leave from the former inspector; Kui having reached office several months later, then returned it;
translations.idiomatic: A military aide still carried a forged commission from the previous inspector; Jia Kui voided it months into his tenure;

sentences.zh: 考竟其二千石以下阿縱不如法者，皆舉奏免之。

translations.literal: he investigated to the end those from two-thousand-shi downward who connived and indulged contrary to law, all impeached and memorialized to dismiss them.
translations.idiomatic: then impeached every magistrate who had abetted lawlessness and had them cashiered.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「逵真刺史矣。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Kui is truly an inspector."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor exclaimed, "Now that is a provincial inspector!"

sentences.zh: 」布告天下，當以豫州爲法。

translations.literal: Proclaim it to the realm—Yu Province should be taken as model."
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the story broadcast so every region might imitate Yu Province."

sentences.zh: 赐爵關内侯。

translations.literal: He was granted noble rank as Neighbourhood Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kui received a neighborhood marquisate.

sentences.zh: 吳將張婴、王崇率眾降。

translations.literal: Wu generals Zhang Ying and Wang Chong led their masses to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu officers Zhang Ying and Wang Chong brought their commands over to Wei.

sentences.zh: 太和二年，帝使逵督前將軍满宠、東莞太守胡質等四軍，從西陽直向東關，曹休從皖，司馬宣王從江陵。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taihe the emperor had Kui supervise Forward General Man Chong, Administrator of Dongguan Hu Zhi, and others in four armies, from Xiyang straight toward Dongguan; Cao Xiu from Wan, Sima Yi from Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 2 the emperor put Jia Kui over four columns—Man Chong, Hu Zhi of Dongguan, and others—driving from Xiyang toward Dongguan while Cao Xiu advanced from Wan and Sima Yi from Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 逵至五將山，休更表贼有请降者，求深入应之。

translations.literal: When Kui reached Wujiang Mountain, Xiu again memorialized that the bandits had some who requested surrender, seeking to go deep and respond to them.
translations.idiomatic: At Wujiang Mountain Cao Xiu reported that enemy deserters begged him to push deep into their lines.

sentences.zh: 詔宣王驻軍，逵東與休合進。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Sima Yi to halt the army; Kui eastward joined Xiu in combined advance.
translations.idiomatic: The court told Sima Yi to stand fast while Jia Kui swung east to reinforce Cao Xiu.

sentences.zh: 逵度贼無東關之備，必並軍於皖；

translations.literal: Kui calculated that the bandits had no preparation at Dongguan—they were sure to combine their army at Wan;
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kui judged that Wu had left Dongguan weak and would mass every spear at Wan;

sentences.zh: 休深入與贼戰，必敗。

translations.literal: Xiu going deep to battle with the bandits was sure to be defeated.
translations.idiomatic: if Cao Xiu drove deep into that trap he would lose.

sentences.zh: 乃部署諸將，水陆並進，行二百里，得生贼，言休戰敗，权遣兵断夹石。

translations.literal: Thereupon he deployed the various generals, by water and land together advancing, marched two hundred li, captured a living bandit who said Xiu had been defeated in battle and Quan had sent troops to cut off Jiashi.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore marched land and water two hundred li, took a Wu prisoner who confirmed Cao Xiu's defeat and Sun Quan's blocking force at Jiashi.

sentences.zh: 諸將不知所出，或欲待後軍。

translations.literal: The various generals did not know what to do; some wished to wait for the rear army.
translations.idiomatic: His generals hesitated, some urging delay until reinforcements arrived.

sentences.zh: 逵曰：「休兵敗於外，路絕於内，進不能戰，退不得還，安危之機，不及終日。

translations.literal: Kui said: "Xiu's army is defeated outside, the roads cut inside—he cannot advance to fight, cannot retreat and return; the pivot of safety and danger does not await the end of the day.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kui said, "Cao Xiu is broken on the field and his retreat is sealed—he cannot fight on and cannot fall back; he has only hours to live.

sentences.zh: 贼以軍無後继，故至此；

translations.literal: the bandits because the army has no rear continuation, therefore have reached this point;
translations.idiomatic: The enemy presses because they think no second column is coming;

sentences.zh: 今疾進，出其不意，此所謂先人以奪其心也，贼見吾兵必走。

translations.literal: now if we hasten forward, catching them unawares—this is what is called forestalling others to seize their hearts—the bandits seeing our army are sure to flee.
translations.idiomatic: strike now while they least expect it—seize the initiative—and they will scatter at our approach."

sentences.zh: 若待後軍，贼已断險，兵雖多何益！

translations.literal: If we wait for the rear army, the bandits will already have cut the defiles—though troops be many, what use!"
translations.idiomatic: Wait for reinforcements and they will hold every pass—numbers will not help then!"

sentences.zh: 」乃兼道進軍，多設旗鼓爲疑兵，贼見逵軍，遂退。

translations.literal: Thereupon he doubled the road and advanced the army, widely set drums and banners as a decoy host; the bandits seeing Kui's army thereupon withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He forced the march, threw up dummy camps of drum and banner, and the Wu lines melted away before him.

sentences.zh: 逵据夹石，以兵粮给休，休軍乃振。

translations.literal: Kui occupied Jiashi, supplied Xiu with troops and grain, and Xiu's army thereupon revived.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Jiashi, fed Cao Xiu's survivors, and the beaten army found its legs again.

sentences.zh: 初，逵與休不善。

translations.literal: At first Kui and Xiu were not on good terms.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kui and Cao Xiu had long been at odds.

sentences.zh: 黄初中，文帝欲假逵节，休曰：「逵性刚，素侮易諸將，不可爲督。

translations.literal: In the Huangchu period Emperor Wen wished to grant Kui credentials; Xiu said: "Kui's nature is stubborn; he always insults and belittles the various generals—he cannot be commander."
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Pi once meant to give Jia Kui the baton, Cao Xiu objected that he was too abrasive to command peers.

sentences.zh: 」帝乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dropped the idea.

sentences.zh: 及夹石之敗，微逵，休軍幾無救也。

translations.literal: As for the defeat at Jiashi, were it not for Kui, Xiu's army would almost have had no rescue.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jiashi disaster it was clear: without Jia Kui, Cao Xiu's host would have perished to a man.

sentences.zh: 〈魏略曰：休怨逵進迟，乃呵责逵，遂使主者敕豫州刺史往拾棄仗。

translations.literal: The Wei lue says: Xiu resented Kui for advancing slowly and therefore rebuked Kui, then had the registrar order the Inspector of Yu Province to go gather discarded weapons.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei lue adds that Cao Xiu blamed Jia Kui for dawdling, berated him, and ordered the Yu inspector to police the battlefield for abandoned gear.

sentences.zh: 逵恃心直，謂休曰：「本爲國家作豫州刺史，不来相爲拾棄仗也。

translations.literal: Kui relying on his straight heart said to Xiu: "Originally I became Inspector of Yu Province for the state, not to come gather discarded weapons for you."
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kui answered hotly, "I was named inspector for the realm—not to pick up your cast-off arms for you."

sentences.zh: 」乃引軍還。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: He marched his column away.

sentences.zh: 遂與休更相表奏，朝廷雖知逵直，猶以休爲宗室任重，两無所非也。

translations.literal: Thereupon he and Xiu mutually memorialized accusations; though the court knew Kui was straight, still because Xiu was imperial kin bearing heavy responsibility, it faulted neither.
translations.idiomatic: The two men traded memorials of complaint; the court knew Jia Kui was right yet refused to censure an imperial prince.

sentences.zh: 魏書云：休猶挟前意，欲以後期罪逵，逵終無言，時人益以此多逵。

translations.literal: The Wei shu says: Xiu still harbored the old resentment and wished to charge Kui with lateness; Kui to the end had no words—people of the time all the more for this praised Kui.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei shu notes Cao Xiu still meant to punish him for slow marching; Jia Kui never answered back, which only deepened public esteem.

sentences.zh: 習凿齒曰：夫賢人者，外身虚己，内以下物，嫌忌之名，何由而生乎？

translations.literal: Xi Zuochi says: As for a worthy man, he sets self aside and empties himself within, humbling himself to yield to things—how would the name of suspicion and jealousy arise?
translations.idiomatic: Xi Zuochi asks how a true gentleman, who effaces himself to serve the common good, could earn a reputation for petty spite.

sentences.zh: 有嫌忌之名者，必與物爲對，存胜負於己身者也。

translations.literal: Those who have the name of suspicion and jealousy must oppose things, storing victory and defeat in their own persons.
translations.idiomatic: Suspicion grows only in men who treat every issue as a personal contest.

sentences.zh: 若以其私憾敗國殄民，彼雖倾覆，於我何利？

translations.literal: If because of private resentment he defeats the state and destroys the people—though they overturn, what profit to me?
translations.idiomatic: To ruin the state for a private grudge brings the foe down on oneself as well—what gain is that?

sentences.zh: 我苟無利，乘之曷爲？

translations.literal: If I have no profit, why ride on it?
translations.idiomatic: If there is nothing to win, why press the attack?

sentences.zh: 以是稱说，臧获之心耳。

translations.literal: To praise such conduct is the mind of a slave or captive.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who applauds such malice thinks like a bondservant.

sentences.zh: 今忍其私忿而急彼之憂，冒難犯危而免之於害，使功显於明君，惠施於百姓，身登於君子之涂，義愧於敌人之心，雖豺虎猶將不觉所復，而况於曹休乎？

translations.literal: Now to swallow private anger and hurry to the other's worry, brave difficulty and risk danger to free him from harm, causing merit to appear to an enlightened lord, kindness to extend to the hundred surnames, the body to ascend the path of the gentleman, righteousness to shame the enemy's heart—even jackals and tigers would still not know what to repay, how much more Cao Xiu?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Jia Kui swallowed old anger to save a rival, risked his life to pull Cao Xiu from the fire, won credit for his sovereign and relief for the people, walked the high road of honor, and shamed the foe—conduct that would move savage beasts, let alone Cao Xiu.

sentences.zh: 然則济彼之危，所以成我之胜，不计宿憾，所以服彼之心，公義既成，私利亦弘，可謂善爭矣。

translations.literal: Thus saving their crisis thereby completes my victory; not reckoning old hatred thereby subdues their hearts—public righteousness already achieved, private profit also is great—this can be called excelling in contention."
translations.idiomatic: Rescuing him secured Wei's victory; forgetting the feud won his heart—public duty and private gain alike served: that is contention at its noblest."

sentences.zh: 在於未能忘胜之流，不由於此而能济胜者，未之有也。〉

translations.literal: For those who are of the class unable to forget victory, not because of this yet able to achieve victorious rescue—there has never been such."〉
translations.idiomatic: Men who cannot forget petty scores will never pull off such a rescue.〉

sentences.zh: 會病笃，謂左右曰：「受國厚恩，恨不斩孫权以下見先帝。

translations.literal: It happened he was gravely ill; he said to those at his sides: "Receiving the state's deep grace, I regret I could not behead Sun Quan and come below to see the late emperor.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he murmured, "The state loaded me with favors; my only regret is that I could not take Sun Quan's head to lay before the late emperor.

sentences.zh: 丧事一不得有所脩作。

translations.literal: For funeral affairs absolutely do not allow any construction or work."
translations.idiomatic: Let my funeral be plain—no lavish works."

sentences.zh: 」薨，諡曰肅侯。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title Marquis Su.
translations.idiomatic: He died and received the posthumous title Marquis Su—"Solemn."

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：逵時年五十五。〉

translations.literal: The Wei shu says: Kui at the time was fifty-five years old.〉
translations.idiomatic: The Wei shu records he was fifty-five.〉

sentences.zh: 子充嗣。

translations.literal: Son Chong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jia Chong inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 豫州吏民追思之，爲刻石立祠。

translations.literal: The clerks and common people of Yu Province pursued thoughts of him, for him carved stone and erected a shrine.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Yu carved him a stele and built a shrine.

sentences.zh: 青龙中，帝東征，乘辇入逵祠，詔曰：「昨过项，見贾逵碑像，念之怆然。

translations.literal: In the Qinglong period the emperor campaigned east, rode the palanquin into Kui's shrine, and ordered saying: "Yesterday passing Xiang I saw Jia Kui's stele image; thinking of it I was mournful.
translations.idiomatic: During Qinglong Cao Rui's eastern tour took him to Jia Kui's shrine; he said, "Passing Xiang yesterday I saw his statue and was overcome.

sentences.zh: 古人有言，患名之不立，不患年之不長。

translations.literal: The ancients had a saying: worry that one's name is not established, do not worry that one's years are not long."
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said to fear an unmade name, not a short life."

sentences.zh: 逵存有忠勋，没而見思，可謂死而不朽者矣。

translations.literal: Kui alive had loyal merit; dead he is remembered—this can be called dead yet not rotting."
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kui served with loyalty in life and is loved in death—true immortality of reputation."

sentences.zh: 其布告天下，以勸將来。」

translations.literal: Proclaim it to the realm to encourage those who come after."
translations.idiomatic: Let the empire hear it, to hearten those who follow."

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略曰：甘露二年，车驾東征，屯项，復入逵祠下，詔曰：「逵没有遺愛，歷世見祠。

translations.literal: The Wei lue says: In the second year of Ganlu the imperial carriage campaigned east, halted at Xiang, again entered beneath Kui's shrine, ordering saying: "Kui dead left lingering kindness; age after age he is sacrificed to.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei lue records that in Ganlu 2 the emperor halted at Xiang, visited the shrine again, and said, "Jia Kui's kindness outlived him; generation after generation honors him.

sentences.zh: 追聞風烈，朕甚嘉之。

translations.literal: Pursuing hearing of his fierce virtue, We greatly approve."
translations.idiomatic: Hearing anew of his fierce integrity, I am deeply moved."

sentences.zh: 昔先帝東征，亦幸于此，親发德音，褒扬逵美，徘徊之心，益有慨然！

translations.literal: Formerly the late emperor on eastern campaign also favored this place, personally issuing virtuous words, praising Kui's excellence; the heart that lingers—still more is there sighing!"
translations.idiomatic: My father campaigned east and stopped here to praise him; standing where he stood, I feel the same awe."

sentences.zh: 夫礼賢之義，或扫其坟墓，或脩其門閭，所以崇敬也。

translations.literal: As for the meaning of rites toward worthies, some sweep their tombs, some repair their gates and lanes—by this one expresses reverence."
translations.idiomatic: The rites tell us to honor the wise by tending their graves and doorways."

sentences.zh: 其扫除祠堂，有穿漏者补治之。」〉

translations.literal: Sweep and clean the shrine hall; where there is piercing leakage repair it."〉
translations.idiomatic: Sweep his hall and patch every leak in the roof."〉

sentences.zh: 子 充

translations.literal: Son: Chong written with the same graph as sufficiency.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jia Chong.

sentences.zh: 充，咸熙中爲中护軍。

translations.literal: Chong, in the Xianxi period was Central Protector of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Chong rose to central protector of the army under the Xianxi reign.

sentences.zh: 〈《晉諸公赞》曰：充字公閭，甘露中爲大將軍長史。

translations.literal: The Jin Zhugong zan says: Chong's courtesy name was Gonglü; in the Ganlu period he was chief clerk to the grand general.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin Zhugong zan names him Jia Chong, style Gonglü, chief clerk to Sima Zhao in the Ganlu years.

sentences.zh: 高贵鄉公之難，司馬文王赖充以免。

translations.literal: At the disaster to the Duke of Gaoguixiang, Sima Wenwang relied on Chong to escape it.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Mao fell, Sima Zhao depended on Jia Chong to survive the crisis.

sentences.zh: 爲晉室元功之臣，位至太宰，封鲁公。

translations.literal: He became a founding merit minister of the Jin house, his office reached Grand Tutor, enfeoffed Duke of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: He became a pillar of the Jin founding, rose to grand tutor, and was invested duke of Lu.

sentences.zh: 諡曰武公。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Duke Wu.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Duke Wu—"Martial."

sentences.zh: 《魏略列傳》以逵及李孚、杨沛三人爲一卷，今列孚、沛二人继逵後耳。

translations.literal: The Wei lue lie zhuan takes Kui together with Li Fu and Yang Pei as one scroll; now listing Fu and Pei two persons continuing after Kui.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei lue once grouped Jia Kui with Li Fu and Yang Pei; here Li and Yang follow his section.

sentences.zh: ◎孚字子宪，钜鹿人也。

translations.literal: ◎ Fu's courtesy name was Zixian; he was a man of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fu, style Zixian, was a native of Julu.

sentences.zh: 興平中，本郡人民饑困。

translations.literal: In the Xingping period the people of his commandery were hungry and distressed.
translations.idiomatic: During Xingping his home commandery starved.

sentences.zh: 孚爲諸生，當种薤，欲以成计。

translations.literal: Fu being a student, was about to plant scallions, wishing thereby to complete a plan.
translations.idiomatic: As a student Li Fu planted chives, nursing some private scheme.

sentences.zh: 有從索者，亦不與一茎，亦不自食，故時人謂能行意。

translations.literal: When there were those who begged from him, he also did not give one stalk, nor did he himself eat them; therefore people of the time said he could carry out his intention.
translations.idiomatic: Beggars got not a single stalk, nor did he eat them himself—contemporaries said he had iron resolve.

sentences.zh: 後爲吏。

translations.literal: Later he became a clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He later entered clerical service.

sentences.zh: 建安中，袁尚领冀州，以孚爲主簿。

translations.literal: In the Jian'an era Yuan Shang led Ji Province and made Fu chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yuan Shang's Ji governorship he became chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 後尚與其兄谭爭斗，尚出軍詣平原，留别驾审配守鄴城，孚随尚行。

translations.literal: Afterward Shang and his elder brother Tan struggled in fighting; Shang went out with the army toward Pingyuan, left Deputy Administrator Shen Pei to guard Ye city, and Fu followed Shang on the march.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan brothers warred, Yuan Shang marched on Pingyuan, left Shen Pei to hold Ye, and Li Fu rode with him.

sentences.zh: 會太祖圍鄴，尚還欲救鄴。

translations.literal: It happened the Grand Progenitor besieged Ye; Shang returned wishing to rescue Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao then besieged Ye; Yuan Shang turned back to relieve it.

sentences.zh: 行未到，尚疑鄴中守備少，復欲令配知外動止，與孚議所遣。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, Shang feared the garrison inside Ye was small, again wished to have Pei know the outer movements, and with Fu discussed whom to dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Ye's garrison too thin, he needed word inside and discussed couriers with Li Fu.

sentences.zh: 孚答尚言：「今使小人往，恐不足以知外内，且恐不能自達。

translations.literal: Fu answered Shang saying: "Now if you send petty men, I fear it is not enough to know inner and outer, and moreover I fear they cannot reach through themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fu said, "A common messenger will learn nothing and never get through.

sentences.zh: 孚请自往。

translations.literal: Fu requests to go himself."
translations.idiomatic: Let me go myself."

sentences.zh: 」尚問孚：「當何所得？

translations.literal: Shang asked Fu: "What ought you obtain?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shang asked what intelligence he hoped to bring back.

sentences.zh: 」孚曰：「聞鄴圍甚坚，多人則觉，以爲直當將三骑足矣。

translations.literal: Fu said: "I hear the siege of Ye is very tight; many men would be noticed—I think straightway leading three riders is enough."
translations.idiomatic: Li Fu answered, "The ring is tight—a crowd would be spotted; three horsemen can slip through."

sentences.zh: 」尚從其计。

translations.literal: Shang followed his plan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shang agreed.

sentences.zh: 孚自选溫信者三人，不语所之，皆敕使具脯粮，不得持兵仗，各给快馬。

translations.literal: Fu himself selected three men warm and trustworthy, did not tell them where they were going, all ordered them to prepare dried meat and grain, not to hold weapons, each given a swift horse.
translations.idiomatic: He picked three trusted men, told them nothing, issued dried rations, forbade arms, and gave each a fast horse.

sentences.zh: 遂辭尚来南，所在止亭傳。

translations.literal: Thereupon he took leave of Shang and came south, halting at every relay station.
translations.idiomatic: They rode south, halting only at post stations.

sentences.zh: 及到梁淇，使從者斫問事杖三十枚，系著馬邊，自著平上帻，將三骑，投暮詣鄴下。

translations.literal: Reaching Liangqi, he had followers cut thirty clerk-inquiry staves, tie them at the horses' flanks, himself put on a flat cap, led three riders, and at dusk approached below Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Near Liangqi he had thirty court staves cut and lashed to the saddlebags, donned a clerk's cap, and at dusk rode up to the siege lines with three men.

sentences.zh: 是時大將軍雖有禁令，而刍牧者多。

translations.literal: At this time though the grand general had prohibitive orders, yet those cutting grass and herding were many.
translations.idiomatic: Though Cao Cao had forbidden casual traffic, foragers still swarmed the lines.

sentences.zh: 故孚因此夜到，以鼓一中，自稱都督，歷北圍，循表而東，從東圍表，又循圍而南，步步呵责守圍將士，随轻重行其罚。

translations.literal: Therefore Fu for this reason arrived by night, with one drum beat styled himself commander-in-chief, passed the northern siege, followed the outer marker east, from the eastern marker again followed the siege south, step by step rebuked the officers and soldiers guarding the siege, according to light or heavy inflicting their punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fu used the hubbub to slip in by night: one drum tap, a shouted claim to be inspector-general, then a swagger along the north face, east along the cordon, south along the stakes, barking orders and "fining" sentries like a true staff officer.

sentences.zh: 遂歷太祖營前，径南过，從南圍角西折，當章門，復责怒守圍者，收缚之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he passed in front of the Grand Progenitor's camp, went straight south past, from the southern siege corner turned west, reached Zhang Gate, again angrily rebuked those guarding the siege, seized and bound them.
translations.idiomatic: He even paraded past Cao Cao's headquarters, doubled the southwest angle, stormed up to Zhang Gate, and "arrested" the guards for show.

sentences.zh: 因開其圍，驰到城下，呼城上人，城上人以绳引，孚得入。

translations.literal: Thereby he opened their siege line, galloped to below the wall, called those on the wall; the wall people with a rope pulled him up, and Fu was able to enter.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he broke the ring, raced to the walls, and was hauled up by rope.

sentences.zh: 配等見孚，悲喜，鼓譟稱萬歲。

translations.literal: When Pei and others saw Fu, sorrow and joy, drumming and shouting called ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Pei's garrison wept and cheered long life.

sentences.zh: 守圍者以狀聞，太祖笑曰：「此非徒得入也，方且復得出。

translations.literal: Those guarding the siege reported the situation; the Grand Progenitor laughed and said: "This is not only having been able to enter—moreover he will yet be able to come out."
translations.idiomatic: When the report reached Cao Cao he laughed, "That man is not only inside—he will walk out again."

sentences.zh: 」孚事讫欲得還，而顾外圍必急，不可復冒。

translations.literal: When Fu's business was finished he wished to return, but surveying the outer siege was sure to be tight, impossible again to risk.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fu's errand done, he saw no safe way back through the lines.

sentences.zh: 謂己使命當速反，乃阴心计，请配曰：「今城中谷少，無用老弱爲也，不如驱出之以省谷也。

translations.literal: He said his mission ought quickly to return, therefore secretly devised a plan, requested of Pei saying: "Now grain inside the city is little; it is useless to keep old and weak here—better drive them out to save grain."
translations.idiomatic: He told Shen Pei, "Grain is low—expel noncombatants to save food."

sentences.zh: 」配從其计，乃復夜简别得數千人，皆使持白幡，從三門並出降。

translations.literal: Pei followed his plan; thereupon again by night separately selected several thousand people, all had them hold white banners, from three gates together went out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Pei agreed; that night thousands of "civilians" with white flags streamed from three gates as if deserting.

sentences.zh: 又使人人持火，孚乃無何將本所從作降人服，随辈夜出。

translations.literal: Also he had every man hold fire; Fu then without ado led his original followers in the dress of surrendering people, following the crowd went out by night.
translations.idiomatic: Torches lit the exodus while Li Fu and his three men, dressed as refugees, mingled with the throng.

sentences.zh: 時守圍將士，聞城中悉降，火光照曜。

translations.literal: At the time the officers and soldiers guarding the siege, hearing that inside the city had entirely surrendered, fire light blazed bright.
translations.idiomatic: The besiegers, hearing Ye had capitulated, gaped at the blaze.

sentences.zh: 但共觀火，不復视圍。

translations.literal: They only together watched the fire, no longer watched the siege.
translations.idiomatic: They watched the flames and forgot the perimeter.

sentences.zh: 孚出北門，遂從西北角突圍得去。

translations.literal: Fu exited the north gate, thereupon from the northwest corner burst the siege and was able to depart.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fu slipped out the north gate and broke through the northwest cordon.

sentences.zh: 其明，太祖聞孚已得出，抵掌笑曰：「果如吾言也。

translations.literal: The next morning the Grand Progenitor heard Fu had already gotten out, clapped palms and laughed saying: "Indeed as Our words said."
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Cao Cao learned he had escaped and clapped, "Just as I said."

sentences.zh: 」孚比見尚，尚甚欢喜。

translations.literal: Fu compared to when he saw Shang, Shang was very pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Fu rejoined Yuan Shang, the prince rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 會尚不能救鄴，破走至中山，而袁谭又追击尚，尚走。

translations.literal: It happened Shang could not save Ye, was defeated and fled to Zhongshan, while Yuan Tan again pursued Shang in attack, and Shang fled.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shang failed to save Ye, fled to Zhongshan, and was hounded by Yuan Tan.

sentences.zh: 孚與尚相失，遂詣谭，復爲谭主簿，東還平原。

translations.literal: Fu lost contact with Shang, thereupon went to Tan, again became Tan's chief clerk, returned east to Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Separated from his lord, Li Fu entered Yuan Tan's service and returned to Pingyuan as his chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 太祖進攻谭，谭戰死。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor advanced to attack Tan; Tan died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao attacked Yuan Tan and killed him in battle.

sentences.zh: 孚還城，城中雖必降，尚擾亂未安。

translations.literal: Fu returned to the city; though inside the city was sure to surrender, still there was disturbance not yet calm.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fu re-entered Ye while it still seethed with disorder though surrender was certain.

sentences.zh: 孚权宜欲得見太祖，乃骑詣牙門，稱冀州主簿李孚欲口白密事。

translations.literal: Fu expediently wished to be able to see the Grand Progenitor, thereupon rode to the army gate, declaring that Ji Province chief clerk Li Fu wished orally to report a secret affair.
translations.idiomatic: To calm the town he rode to Cao Cao's gate claiming Ji chief clerk Li Fu bore secret word.

sentences.zh: 太祖見之，孚叩头謝。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor saw him; Fu knocked his head in apology.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao received him, and Li Fu kowtowed in apology.

sentences.zh: 太祖問其所白，孚言「今城中强弱相陵，心皆不定，以爲宜令新降爲内所识信者宣傳明教。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor asked what he wished to report orally; Fu said "Now inside the city strong and weak mutually bully, hearts are all not settled—I think it fitting to order those newly surrendered whom those within recognize and trust to spread and proclaim the enlightened instruction."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao asked his business; Li Fu said the city was still divided, strong preying on weak, and proposed that trusted locals among the recent surrenders proclaim the court's amnesty aloud.

sentences.zh: 」公謂孚曰：「卿便還宣之。

translations.literal: The lord said to Fu: "You then return and proclaim it."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao told him, "Go back in and announce it."

sentences.zh: 」孚跪请教，公曰：「便以卿意宣也。

translations.literal: Fu knelt requesting instruction; the lord said: "Straightway use your meaning to proclaim."
translations.idiomatic: Li Fu knelt for wording; Cao Cao said, "Say whatever you think right."

sentences.zh: 」孚還入城，宣教「各安故業，不得相侵陵。

translations.literal: Fu returned into the city, proclaiming instruction "each settle in former occupation, must not mutually invade or bully."
translations.idiomatic: He re-entered Ye and proclaimed that every household should return to its trade and molest no neighbor.

sentences.zh: 」城中以安，乃還报命，公以孚爲良足用也。

translations.literal: Inside the city thereby was pacified; he then returned to report completion of orders; the lord because of Fu thought him truly sufficient to use.
translations.idiomatic: Order returned; he reported back, and Cao Cao marked him as a man to rely on.

sentences.zh: 會爲所間，裁署冗散。

translations.literal: It happened he was slandered in between, was appointed only to redundant and scattered posts.
translations.idiomatic: Slander soon relegated him to idle sinecures.

sentences.zh: 出守解長，名爲严能。

translations.literal: He went out to guard as chief of Xie, his name was stern capability.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as magistrate of Xie, famed for harsh efficiency.

sentences.zh: 稍遷至司隶校尉，時年七十餘矣，其於精断無衰，而术略不損於故。

translations.literal: Gradually he was promoted to Colonel Director of Retainers; at the time he was more than seventy years old; as to keen judgment there was no decline, while stratagem and planning did not diminish from former.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to metropolitan commandant past seventy, as sharp in judgment as ever and as cunning as in youth.

sentences.zh: 終於陽平太守。

translations.literal: He ended as Administrator of Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office as prefect of Yangping.

sentences.zh: 孚本姓冯，後改爲李。

translations.literal: Fu's original surname was Feng; afterward changed to Li.
translations.idiomatic: His clan had been Feng; he later took the surname Li.

sentences.zh: ◎杨沛字孔渠，冯翊萬年人也。

translations.literal: ◎ Yang Pei, courtesy name Kongqu, was a native of Wannian in Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Pei, style Kongqu, came from Wannian in Fengyi commandery.

sentences.zh: 初平中，爲公府令史，以牒除爲新郑長。

translations.literal: In the Chuping period he was a clerk of the ducal offices, by memorial was appointed magistrate of Xinzheng.
translations.idiomatic: During Chuping he served the warlord's chancellery and was posted magistrate of Xinzheng on written recommendation.

sentences.zh: 興平末，人多饑窮，沛课民益畜乾椹，收幪豆，阅其有餘以补不足，如此积得千餘斛，藏在小仓。

translations.literal: At the end of Xingping many people were hungry and destitute; Pei taxed the people to increase stores of dried mulberries, gathered bean pods, examined those who had surplus to supplement those insufficient—thus accumulating more than a thousand hu, stored in a small granary.
translations.idiomatic: At the close of Xingping he taxed his people not in coin but in dried mulberries and beans, pooling surplus to feed the hungry until he had a thousand hu cached in a granary.

sentences.zh: 會太祖爲兗州刺史，西迎天子，所將千餘人皆無粮。

translations.literal: It happened the Grand Progenitor was Inspector of Yanzhou, going west to welcome the Son of Heaven; those he led, more than a thousand men, all lacked grain.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao marched west as Yanzhou inspector to escort the emperor, his thousand-man column arrived starving.

sentences.zh: 过新郑，沛謁見，乃皆進乾椹。

translations.literal: Passing Xinzheng, Pei had audience, then all presented dried mulberries.
translations.idiomatic: At Xinzheng Yang Pei presented the whole stock of dried mulberries.

sentences.zh: 太祖甚喜。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor was very pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao was delighted.

sentences.zh: 及太祖辅政，遷沛爲長社令。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor assisted government, he promoted Pei to be chief of Changshe.
translations.idiomatic: Once Cao Cao held the capital, he moved Yang Pei to magistrate of Changshe.

sentences.zh: 時曹洪宾客在縣界，徵調不肯如法，沛先挝折其脚，遂杀之。

translations.literal: At the time Cao Hong's guests were within the county borders; on levy and requisition they refused to comply with the law; Pei first beat and broke their legs, then killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Guests of Cao Hong refused lawful levy; Yang Pei broke their legs, then executed them.

sentences.zh: 由此太祖以爲能。

translations.literal: Thereby the Grand Progenitor thought him capable.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao judged him indispensable.

sentences.zh: 累遷九江、東平、乐安太守，並有治迹。

translations.literal: Accumulating promotions he became Administrator of Jiujiang, Dongping, and Lean; all had traces of good order.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through prefectures of Jiujiang, Dongping, and Lean, each time leaving a record of firm rule.

sentences.zh: 坐與督軍爭斗，髡刑五歲。

translations.literal: Because of sitting in quarrel and fight with the army supervisor, he received shaved-head punishment for five years.
translations.idiomatic: A brawl with an army inspector earned him five years' penal labor with shaved head.

sentences.zh: 输作未竟，會太祖出征在谯，聞鄴下颇不奉科禁，乃发教选鄴令，當得严能如杨沛比，故沛從徒中起爲鄴令。

translations.literal: Corvée labor not yet finished, it happened the Grand Progenitor was on campaign at Qiao, heard that below Ye largely did not uphold statutes and prohibitions, thereupon issued an order to select a Ye magistrate—must obtain stern capability like Yang Pei's sort—therefore Pei from among convict laborers was raised to be Ye magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: While still in the labor gang he was plucked for duty because Cao Cao, camped at Qiao, heard Ye was lawless and demanded a magistrate as ruthless as Yang Pei.

sentences.zh: 已拜，太祖見之，問曰：「以何治鄴？

translations.literal: After the appointment was conferred, the Grand Progenitor saw him and asked saying: "By what means will you govern Ye?"
translations.idiomatic: At his audience Cao Cao asked, "How will you rule Ye?"

sentences.zh: 」沛曰：「竭尽心力，奉宣科法。

translations.literal: Pei said: "Exhaust heart and strength, reverently proclaim statutes and laws."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Pei answered, "With every ounce of zeal I will enforce your code."

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「善。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao said, "Good."

sentences.zh: 」顾謂坐席曰：「諸君，此可畏也。

translations.literal: He looked back and said to those seated on mats: "Gentlemen, this one is to be feared."
translations.idiomatic: He turned to his courtiers and said, "Gentlemen, fear this man."

sentences.zh: 」赐其生口十人，绢百匹，既欲以励之，且以报乾椹也。

translations.literal: He granted him ten living captives, one hundred bolts of silk—both wishing thereby to encourage him, and also to repay the dried mulberries.
translations.idiomatic: He gave him ten captives, a hundred bolts of silk—to reward his zeal and repay the mulberries.

sentences.zh: 沛辭去，未到鄴，而軍中豪右曹洪、刘勋等畏沛名，遣家

translations.literal: Pei took leave and departed; before he reached Ye, the army grandees Cao Hong, Liu Xun, and others, fearing Pei's reputation, sent household servants
translations.idiomatic: Before Yang Pei reached Ye, great families such as Cao Hong and Liu Xun, dreading his reputation, sent household messengers

sentences.zh: （驰骑）

translations.literal: (galloping; gloss in the text)
translations.idiomatic: riding at full gallop

sentences.zh: 〔骑驰〕告子弟，使各自检敕。

translations.literal: [variant order] to inform sons and younger brothers, making each examine and restrain himself.
translations.idiomatic: to warn sons and nephews to straighten out their conduct before the new magistrate arrived.

sentences.zh: 沛爲令數年，以功能轉爲护羌都尉。

translations.literal: Pei being magistrate several years, by merit and function was transferred to Colonel Director of the Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: After some years as magistrate he was promoted colonel of the Qiang.

sentences.zh: 十六年，馬超反，大軍西讨，沛随軍，都督孟津渡事。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Ma Chao rebelled; the great army campaigned west to punish him; Pei followed the army, supervised the affair of Mengjin ford crossing.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, when Ma Chao rebelled, Yang Pei followed the host and directed the crossing at Mengjin.

sentences.zh: 太祖已南过，其餘未毕，而中黄門前渡，忘持行轩，私北還取之，從吏求小船，欲独先渡。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor had already crossed south; the remainder was not finished, but a palace yellow gate who crossed earlier forgot to hold the traveling canopy, privately returned north to fetch it, requested a small boat from the clerk, wishing alone to cross first.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao had already crossed when a eunuch turned back for a forgotten palanquin canopy and demanded a private boat to overtake the army.

sentences.zh: 吏呵不肯，黄門與吏爭言。

translations.literal: The clerk shouted and would not agree; the yellow gate quarreled in speech with the clerk.
translations.idiomatic: The river clerk refused; the eunuch argued.

sentences.zh: 沛問黄門：「有疏邪？

translations.literal: Pei asked the yellow gate: "Do you have a written order?"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Pei demanded, "Where is your written order?"

sentences.zh: 」黄門云：「無疏。

translations.literal: The yellow gate said: "There is no written order."
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch admitted he had none.

sentences.zh: 」沛怒曰：「何知汝不欲逃邪？

translations.literal: Pei angrily said: "How do I know you do not wish to flee?"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Pei shouted, "For all I know you are deserting!"

sentences.zh: 」遂使人捽其头，與杖欲捶之，而逸得去，衣帻皆裂坏，自诉于太祖。

translations.literal: Thereupon he had people seize his head, together with a staff wished to beat him, but he escaped and got away, clothes and cap all torn and ruined, personally complained to the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: He had the man seized and raised a club; the eunuch broke loose in torn clothes and ran to Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「汝不死爲幸矣。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor said: "That you did not die is fortunate."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao told the eunuch, "You are lucky Yang Pei did not kill you."

sentences.zh: 」由是声名益振。

translations.literal: Thereby his fame and voice the more shook.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Pei's name rang louder than ever.

sentences.zh: 及關中破，代張既领京兆尹。

translations.literal: When Guanzhong was broken, he replaced Zhang Ji in leading the Governor of the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: After Guanzhong fell he succeeded Zhang Ji as governor of the capital district.

sentences.zh: 黄初中，儒雅並進，而沛本以事能見用，遂以議郎冗散里巷。

translations.literal: In the Huangchu period Confucian refinement together advanced, but Pei originally because of administrative ability was employed, thereupon as Consultant Counselor was redundant and scattered in lanes and alleys.
translations.idiomatic: Under Huangchu's literary fashion a rough administrator like him was shelved as a consultant and left to rot in the lanes.

sentences.zh: 沛前後宰歷城守，不以私计介意，又不肯以事贵人，故身退之後，家無餘积。

translations.literal: Pei before and after had been chief of cities and guards, did not take private schemes to heart, also was unwilling to use affairs to flatter the noble—therefore after his person retired, the household had no surplus accumulation.
translations.idiomatic: He had never lined his pockets, never flattered the mighty, and so retired penniless.

sentences.zh: 治疾於家，借舍從兒，無他奴婢。

translations.literal: Treating illness at home, he borrowed lodging from a nephew's house, having no other slave girls.
translations.idiomatic: Ill at the end, he lodged with a nephew and kept no servants.

sentences.zh: 後占河南

translations.literal: Later he registered a claim in Henan
translations.idiomatic: Later he registered a claim to wasteland in Henan

translations.literal: (The manuscript reads 夕, probably for 西 'west' in the placename Xiyang.)
translations.idiomatic: where the characters 河南夕 appear corrupt (夕 probably stands for 西 in the placename Xiyang)

sentences.zh: 陽亭部荒田二顷，起瓜牛庐，居止其中，其妻子冻饿。

translations.literal: waste fields of two qing in the Xiyang station precinct; he raised a melon-herder's hut, dwelt and stopped within it; his wife and children froze and starved.
translations.idiomatic: two qing of abandoned fields in the Xiyang postal precinct; he threw up a brushwood hut, lived in it, and his wife and children went cold and hungry.

sentences.zh: 沛病亡，鄉人親友及故吏民爲殡葬也。〉

translations.literal: Pei died of illness; village people, kin, friends, and former clerks and commoners for him conducted burial.〉
translations.idiomatic: When he died, neighbors and old subordinates pooled what they had to bury him.〉

translations.literal: 【Appraisal】
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal

sentences.zh: 评曰：自漢季以来，刺史總統諸郡，賦政于外，非若曩時司察之而已。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: From the end of Han onward, inspectors general-presided over the various commanderies, assessing government outside the capital—not like earlier times when they were only investigators.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Late Han turned provincial inspectors into regional governors who wielded real power abroad, not mere auditors of old.

sentences.zh: 太祖創基，迄終魏業，此皆其流稱誉有名實者也。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor founded the base, down to the end of Wei enterprise—these all are those who in the current bore praise and had name matching reality.
translations.idiomatic: From Cao Cao's founding through Wei's end, the men in this scroll earned reputations that matched their deeds.

sentences.zh: 咸精達事機，威恩兼著，故能肅齊萬里，見述於後也。

translations.literal: All were keen through the pivot of affairs, awe and kindness both manifest; therefore they were able to bring order across ten thousand li and be narrated by those who came after.
translations.idiomatic: Each mastered the moment, blended severity with mercy, and so kept the frontiers quiet for generations to remember.
